articleTitle: Basic Study of Deep Learning Based Efficient Hermit Crabs Detection from Drone-Captured Images
abstract: The challenges arising from water clarity, depth, and other factors intensify the difficulties in surveying underwater hermit crabs, exacerbated by a notable shortage of practical field surveys. This study introduces a novel approach utilizing consumer-grade Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and deep learning to investigate underwater hermit crabs. We applied diverse super-resolution algorithms, employing distinct design strategies for image enhancement. Furthermore, we utilized the proposed object detection model developed from YOLOv8, achieving a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.722, surpassing other state-of-the-art object detection algorithms. Applying UAVs and super-resolution technology has significantly progressed underwater hermit crab detection, providing practical solutions for aquatic ecological monitoring, and enabling precise benthos detection.

articleTitle: Channel Model for Massive MIMO Shallow Underwater Acoustic Communications
abstract: Oceans are an environment attracting growing interest, with major economic stakes. There exists a need to design systems able to explore the underwater environment, one of the challenges being the ability to communicate undersea. The underwater acoustic channel is considered as being one of the most difficult environments for designing communication systems, due to multiple limitations (frequency band, latency, Doppler effect …). A method that could allow an increase of the data rate is the use of massive MIMO (multiple inputs, multiple outputs) systems, where many transducers are used to emit as well as to receive the signal. The objective of this paper is to present a model for a massive MIMO underwater acoustic communication channel in order to carry out a preliminary analysis of the impact of array correlation on the theoretical achievable rate by using Shannon capacity.

articleTitle: A Feasibility Study on Novel View Synthesis of Underwater Structures using Neural Radiance Fields
abstract: We explore Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) for synthesizing novel views of underwater structures. This learning-based approach relies on a sparse set of camera views to model the 3D geometry of underwater structures and scenes. Real-world underwater scenes exhibit significant temporal variations, introducing challenges in maintaining visual consistency. We investigate three NeRF implementations: 1) nerfacto, which rep-resents the baseline; 2) nerfacto with transient embed dings and 3) nerfacto with a robust loss, which are designed to deal with scene inconsistencies. We evaluate these implementations using datasets collected in 1) a controlled environment and 2) a real underwater setting. The modified implementations consistently outperform the original nerfacto across both datasets. The performance im-provements are particularly pronounced in the dataset obtained from the real underwater setting where scene inconsistencies are more prevalent. This underscores the importance of robustifying NeRF implementations to ensure consistent performance in the challenging underwater environments.

articleTitle: Long-Term Forecasting of Ocean Sound Speeds at any time via Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
abstract: Long-term forecasting of ocean sound speed is crucial for underwater sound propagation. Traditional sound speed forecasting models include auto-regressive models and deep neural networks. They have two shortcomings: 1) they lack interpretability and cannot perform long-term forecasting; 2) they cannot forecast sound speed at any time. To overcome the shortcomings, this paper presents a novel approach that utilizes neural ordinary differential equations (ODEs), a recent continuous neural network model, to forecast the sound speed at any time. Specifically, this paper proposes a round-by-round training approach that avoids being trapped in poor local optima. This paper uses Shallow Water (SW) 06 sea trial data for the experiment. The results indicate that the proposed Neural ODE sound speed forecasting model is more effective in long-term forecasting than traditional models and can forecast sound speed at any time accurately.

Author Keywords: Long-term forecasting of ocean sound speed

articleTitle: Braids, Knots and Links: Investigating Dynamic Human Features as Geometric Proxies for Supervised Feature Extraction in Different Ocean Acoustic Applications
abstract: Robust feature representation and its training and testing has been an ongoing challenge for autonomous sonar target recognition for decades. Key challenges include but are not limited to: unpredictable acoustic scatter from non-target reflectors within the oceanic environment, underwater acoustic multipath scattering, as well as unknown feature distortions due to uncertainties in target geometry. What has been seldom explored is the geometry between the target features themselves, which often overlap nonlinearly, with each other as well as across non-target features from the underwater acoustic environment. These geometries also change dynamically as a function of time, frequency, angle, cross-range, and other parameters important for sonar considerations. While machine learning techniques, both physics-inspired and black-box architectures, have been employed to discover and track these inherent features, not enough has been done to investigate the morphing geometries of these features in a systematic quantitative sense. In this position paper, we explore this question from the perspective of dynamic geometric proxies inherent in dancing human features and other artistic and natural structures, and use these as model props to study abstract geometric constructs such as braids, knots and links. The end goal is to create robust ground truths for these geometric constructs that are meaningful in sonar feature discovery and interpretation. The key idea is to exploit the geometry inherent in these structures as a means of creating innovative augmented data repositories for training and testing active sonar features. We present some geometric examples using video stills and discuss our observations on the promise and challenges of this training and testing simulation method.

articleTitle: A Stable Chebyshev-Padé Rational Approximation of Parabolic Equation Models for Underwater Sound Field Computation
abstract: A stable Chebyshev-Padé rational approximation method of parabolic equation models is developed by introducing stability constraints into a Chebyshev type rational approximation. Operator analysis in theory is taken and demonstrates the good performance of the proposed approximation on accuracy, efficiency and stability. Numerical results in two ocean acoustic cases including a shallow water slope benchmark problem and propagation problem under a deep water seamounts environment in the South China Sea support that the stable Chebyshev-Padé rational approximation is suitable for underwater sound field computation.

articleTitle: Doppler-Shift Tolerant Digital Modulation and Demodulation Scheme for Fast Moving Underwater Acoustic Communication Systems
abstract: Reliable communication in underwater acoustic channels is a challenge task because various kind of factors such as multipath interference, Doppler shift, and ambient noise should be considered. This paper presents a new digital modulation and demodulation scheme called as stretchable symbols with multiple sequences (SSMS) that can work under both low SNR and large Doppler scale conditions. The key idea is to demodulate by FFT-based cross correlation without compensating received signals. The position of FFT window can be changed in response to signal expansion and contraction caused by non-uniform Doppler shifts. The effectiveness of SSMS has been demonstrated in the sea trial with the relative speed of 10 knot (5.1 m/s).

articleTitle: Sediment characterization using seabed seismic measurements
abstract: Data from Seabed Characterization Experiment (SBCEX-2022) conducted at the New England Mud Patch (NEMP) off the United States East Coast are analyzed in this study. Broadband Signal, Underwater Sound (SUS) sources were deployed as part of this experiment. Acoustic pressure and three components of particle motion from the SUS deployments were measured on seismic sensor packages (OBX). Polarization analysis using Stokes parameter framework is carried out to highlight the transverse components. The sensitivity of one of the Stokes parameters to modal attenuation is also investigated. Preliminary results, which compare well with previous studies, are also presented.

Index Terms: East Coast Of The United States

articleTitle: Energy-Balanced Clustering Protocols for Underwater Sensor Networks
abstract: Underwater sensor networks(USNs) play a vital role in marine devices, which work under energy -constrained environments. Numerous network clustering algorithms have been proposed to enhance the network lifespan. However, existing network clustering algorithms generally select cluster heads(CHs) randomly, which leads to uneven clustering results, imbalanced energy consumption in the network. In this paper, we present a spectral-clustering-based USN clustering strategy(SCUC), which achieves uniform clustering of network nodes, effectively balancing the energy consumption and prolonging the network lifespan. We also have verified its superiority through simulations.

articleTitle: An Architecture for Virtual Tethering of ROVs
abstract: We introduce an architecture designed for wireless Remote Operated Vehicle (ROV) operations during intervention surveys. Using the recent advancements in 3D modeling, visual odometry, video compression, and underwater communication, our approach aims to facilitate fully wireless ROV operations. The proposed architecture comprises several modular blocks, each with versatile applications spanning diverse domains, including multiplayer gaming, remote rover control and video transmission over a low-bandwidth connection. This comprehensive framework signifies progress in ROV operations, replacing the traditional physical tether with a software-defined virtual tether.

articleTitle: Simulation of High-Speed Vessel Waves Based on 2D+t SPH Method
abstract: In this article, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathrm{D}+\mathrm{t}$</tex> SPH method is used to simulate the bow wave which generate by a high-speed vessel, and observed the process of wave flipping, breaking, and details of air entrainment. The results show that the SPH method has unique advantages in simulating breaking wave, and in addition, for high-speed slender vessels, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathrm{D}+\mathrm{T}$</tex> theory can provide a relatively accurate process of wave evolution while significantly reducing computational complexity.

articleTitle: Enhanced Kalman Equalization via Channel Prediction for Single-Carrier MIMO Underwater Acoustic Communications
abstract: For single-carrier underwater acoustic (UWA) communications, a Kalman equalizer (KE) is a promising receiver scheme with decent performance-complexity tradeoff. On one hand, it outperforms a direct adaptive equalizer (DAE). On the other hand, its computational complexity is one magnitude lower than that of a conventional channel estimation based equalizer (CEE). Even though, the KE has to make a delayed decision so as to achieve satisfactory performance under multipath UWA channels. Such a decision delay incurs a lag in channel es-timation, which leads to performance degradation under fast-varying channel conditions. To address this issue, we propose an enhanced Kalman equalization scheme via channel prediction in this paper. Based on channel estimations available at the current time, channels at future times are predicted via a cubic spline interpolation method such that KE can be performed beyond current time. Both simulated and at-sea experimental results are provided, verifying the performance gain of the proposed KE with channel prediction over existing solutions.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of an Underwater Imaging Method using a Moving Single Acoustic Vector Sensor and Acoustic Source
abstract: A single acoustic vector sensor (AVS) senses the acoustic pressure and 3D particle velocity components. Its advantage over an omni-directional hydrophone or even a hydrophone array are well known. Its disadvantages mainly stem from practical considerations such as effect of flow noise etc. that are being steadily overcome, making the sensor useful for applications in which hydrophone arrays are traditionally used. There is hardly any previous reported work on the use of AVS for underwater imaging that is the subject of this paper. This work aims at studying the potential of a single AVS in motion along with an acoustic projector for the purpose of underwater imaging. Specifically, the paper reports the imaging capabilities with a low cost and low complexity sensor system. The approach is to transmit a triangularly frequency modulated (TFM) signal from an acoustic projector and receive the scatter returns from the objects in the field of view (FOV) on an AVS. Both projector and AVS are mounted on a compact moving underwater vessel such as an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) or remotely operated vehicle (ROV). The algorithm maps Doppler information in the received signal to the azimuth and elevation angles in the FOV and the range from travel time in the particular direction. The diversity due to 4 channels of the AVS is used to create a 3D image. The algorithm is able to identify scatter returns from about 1<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ$</tex> separation in azimuth and elevation directions. The feasibility of the method for underwater imaging has been investigated through simulation studies that are reported in this paper.

articleTitle: Wave Excitation Force Estimation for Wave Energy Converters Using Square Root Unscented Kalman Filters
abstract: In wave energy converters (WECs), operative control strategies require the wave excitation force to be known and available in real time. Unfortunately, the force is immeasurable and can only be estimated from other measurable quantities. This paper proposes a square root unscented Kalman filter (SR-UKF) to estimate the wave excitation force acting on a heaving WEC. The estimator depends on available measurements of the WEC mechanical states and has the ability to incorporate WEC nonlinearities. The SR-UKF estimation performance is tested under several sea state scenarios and verified through MATLAB simulation. The SR-UKF exhibits satisfactory estimation accuracy, with a goodness of fit between 98.5% - 93.4% for all investigated scenarios.

articleTitle: Development of a Jellyfish Removal Device to Equip on Underwater Robot and Its Suction Performance Evaluation
abstract: In recent years, massive blooms of jellyfish have occurred due to the influence of rising water temperatures, causing damage to industries such as fisheries. To reduce the damage caused by jellyfish, fishermen conduct jellyfish removal work, however, it cannot be said to be efficient from a cost perspective. As one of the efficient methods, our research team is proposing an underwater robot-based jellyfish removal work. Our research team has developed a small-size underwater robot to test, and with the assistance of the fisheries workers, conducted jellyfish removal tests in the Seto Inland Sea in August 2022. Through this test, we confirmed that jellyfish removal using underwater robots is feasible, and based on the results of the test, we improved the jellyfish removal device. In this paper, we introduce the improved jellyfish removal devices, that we have developed, and then evaluate the performance of this device. In the results of the performance evaluation, compared to the test type device, the improved device showed a suction range that was 2.77 times wider, and the flow velocity increased by 2.28 times.

articleTitle: Distributed BSP Control Methods for Underwater Collective Manipulation
abstract: We have developed a novel cooperative manipulation approach exploiting the compliance of the 'grippers' and a Reynolds boids' collective coordinated movement implemented, by exploiting Belief Space Planning (BSP) to enforce the Reynolds' flock rules.

articleTitle: A Positioning Method Based on Path Control of Multiple Autonomous Underwater Vehicles
abstract: This study proposes a method in which an AUV equipped with a low-precision navigation sensor (child AUV) performs more accurate and stable positioning using acoustic relative positioning information with a positioning reference AUV (parent AUV). In an underwater environment, acoustic positioning communications are susceptible to disturbances, which can cause the parent and child AUVs to lose communication. This is relatively common in underwater environments and once communication is lost, it is difficult to recover it. Therefore, to maintain communication, this study proposes a method to predict the situation in which communication is likely to be lost. It is expected that operating multiple AUVs while maintaining their positional relation will increase the accuracy and stability of position estimation. In the proposed method, the child AUV continuously records the distance of the parent AUV and approaches the parent AUV to decrease the distance if it tends to increase. A particle filter is used for state estimation. The performance of the proposed method was evaluated through navigation simulation. The results of the experiments showed that the proposed method can maintain a stable position relation with reliable uninterrupted communication between multiple AUVs.

articleTitle: Numerical Research on the Effect of Propeller Rotation Direction on the Propulsion Performance and Load Difference of Inner and Outer Propeller in a Four-Screw Ship
abstract: In the actual sailing of the four-screw ship, due to the asymmetrically distributed wake, the inner propeller and outer propeller show obvious load difference. The load difference will affect the machine-propeller matching and reduce the service life of the main engine. This paper proposes a method to reduce the load difference by changing the rotation direction of the inner and outer propellers. The RANS method is used in this paper to simulate the self-propulsion of a four-screw ship with different rotational arrangements. By analyzing the propeller load variation, the propeller and wake flow interrelationships are illustrated. The peak value of the main propeller blade is related to the circumferential velocity distribution. When the inner and outer propellers are rotating inward at the same time, the efficiency of the inner propeller is increased and the torque difference between inner and outer propellers is reduced to within 1%, the lateral loads are reduced by 15% to 40%.

articleTitle: Adaptive Real-Time Video Transmission Through Underwater Acoustic Communication Link
abstract: Efficient video transmission enables a wide range of applications in underwater environments, such as seabed survey, subsea equipment maintenance, oil pipe/bridge inspection, and marine life sample collection. At present, it is a common belief that real-time underwater video transmission through underwater acoustic communication is challenging due to the influence of complex underwater environments and the limitation of underwater acoustic communication. In this paper, we propose an adaptive real-time underwater video transmission system using underwater communication. The system consists of three modules, i.e, video pre-processing module, video transmission module and video post-processing module. In the first two modules, the sender adaptively adjusts the compression bitrate and transmission rate according to the video quality and channel conditions. In the third module, the deep learning-based video reconstruction algorithm for underwater image information recovery is exploited. The efficacy of this system is verified by real underwater videos collected in several sea fields. The results prove the proposed system is able to transmit video successfully and efficiently in the underwater environment.

articleTitle: Study on the Degradation of Acoustic Waveforms used for GNSS-A Observations
abstract: This study examines the degradation of acoustic waveforms in the seafloor crustal movement observation network called Seafloor Geodetic Observation – Array (SGO-A) operated by the Japan Coast Guard using Global Navigation Satellite System - Acoustics combination (GNSS-A) technology. Recently, it was found that the 10 kHz carrier wave used was distorted, resulting in a loss of accuracy. Misidentification of carrier waves due to distortion occurs on a scale of several to 20 cm and significantly hinders centimeter-level observations of vertical positioning. In this study, conducted in an experimental tank, the transmitted waveforms were investigated using the Phase-Only Correlation (POC) method with equipment similar to that used for actual observations. The results suggested that the waveform degradation was mainly due to the superposition of multiple reference waves. In order to evaluate the cause of the carrier wave degradation, a grid-search-like method was used to reproduce the degraded carrier wave. It was shown that the degradation of the carrier wave was not only caused by the hardware structure, but mainly by the internal electrical circuit. These findings suggest the need to examine waveform degradation phenomenon in detail with each equipment and other conditions to determine accurate round-trip times.

articleTitle: Research on Acoustic Target Strength Based on Graphical Acoustic Computing Method
abstract: A graphical acoustic computing method (GRACO) based on Kirchhoff approximation is introduced for the problem of acoustic backscattering in underwater structures. On this basis, an impedance sphere is taken as the research object, and the target strength is calculated using the partial wave series, boundary element method, and GRACO, respectively. The results show that GRACO has sufficient accuracy in the high frequency range. While compared to other methods, the computational efficiency of GRACO is significantly superior. Subsequently, GRACO is used to predict the target strength of the main hull of the BeTSSi model. The study show that the composite material has the lowest target strength, followed by titanium alloy, and the steel structure has the highest target strength.

articleTitle: A Novel UAC Modem Design with Two Core Modules
abstract: Underwater acoustic communication (UAC) modem is one of the key components of underwater acoustic sensor networks. In order to reduce the system power consumption, the cost, and the difficulty of development, and satisfy different communication requirements, a novel embedded UAC modem with adaptive modulation, positioning, and networking function is designed. The STM32F413 chip with low power and low cost, as well as Raspberry Pi Zero 2W with high computing speed and convenience of development, are used as the core processing units collectively, to ensure high computing speed and low power consumption of the system. The solution is flexible, and can be developed and extended according to different communication requirements in future. Experiment results show that the UAC modem can realize reliable communication of 100 bps-1 kbps in the distance of 6–8 km.

articleTitle: Towards Low-Cost and Energy-Optimized Underwater Image Classification Based-on FPGA
abstract: Based on deep learning, image classification has become widely popular in the field of underwater vision. However, due to the unique underwater environment, GPU-based image classification methods face challenges in power consumption and resource utilization. To address these issues, we propose an FPGA-based underwater image classification method. The method includes a cyclic blocking technique for convolutional computation, effectively improving resource utilization. We also design an efficient storage architecture, utilizing on-chip FPGA memory to achieve optimal energy consumption for underwater classification models. Additionally, we enhance computational efficiency by setting up pipelined computation in the convolutional cyclic blocks. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves significantly lower power consumption while maintaining low hardware resource utilization. The power consumption is 8.5 watts for ResNet34 and 4.6 watts for VGG16. This method is particularly suitable for vision-based underwater devices.

articleTitle: Portable and Flexible Seabed Station with a Fly-Out Vehicle
abstract: Seabed observatories or stations are specialized research facilities designed to monitor and study various aspects of the ocean environment. They are essential tools for advancing our knowledge of the oceans and their interconnected processes. Technologically, seabed stations are multi-sensor instrumentation modules, made for long-term deployment and designed to measure various physical, chemical, biological variables in a marine environment. This paper presents Subsea Station developed at Applied Underwater Robotic Laboratory (AURLab) Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU). Development goal was to design portable Seabed Station with flexible instrumentation configuration and integrated mobile sensor platform, fly-out vehicle. Concept of Resident Vehicles (fly-out vehicles) is usually related to bigger, work class vehicles. Therefore, specific novelty of this concept is integration of an observation/mini-class fly-out vehicle into the subsea station. The paper presents the concept, metodology and results of the preliminary tests. Further testing and long-term deployment are expected during the 2024.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of an AUV with Dual Acoustic Communication Modems
abstract: In this paper, a method for designing and fabricating an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) with a dual Acoustic Communication Modem is presented. The aim is to ensure reli-able communication in challenging underwater environments. To achieve this, the AUV incorporates two underwater communication modems that use the FKS-FH and PSK-OFDM methods. The proposed AUV also includes a combined inertial measurement unit (IMU) and Doppler velocity log (DVL) navigation system, as well as a non-linear controller. These features enable stable navigation and the collection of topographical information from the seabed. Real-world sea trials were conducted to validate the AUV's performance in terms of precise control, stability, underwater communication, and navigation. The success rate and maximum communication distance of the underwater communication system were calculated. Furthermore, real-field tests were carried out to confirm the system's reliable underwater commu-nication and navigation capabilities. The successful integration of advanced navigation systems and underwater communication technologies into the AUV demonstrates its potential for complex marine tasks and operations.

articleTitle: Underwater Robot with Bioinspired Multimodal Locomotion Expands the Scope of Ocean Exploration
abstract: The exploration of underwater environments presents unique challenges that conventional propeller-based underwater robots struggle to overcome due to their inherent limitations in maneuverability and environmental disturbance. This has lead to the interest in bioinspired robotic systems capable of multimodal locomotion, inspired by the versatile movements of marine animals that excel in both swimming and benthic locomotion. This article introduces the design framework of a novel bioinspired underwater vehicle, RoboIguana, which draws inspiration from the marine iguana's ability to perform both undulatory swimming and benthic legged locomotion. We present in detail the design of different subsystems of the robot, including legged and swimming locomotion, vision, electronics, and chassis. The integration of these subsystems aims to enable RoboIguana to navigate complex underwater terrains effectively, offering an innovative tool for marine exploration and research.

articleTitle: Flexible and Compact Animal-Borne Sensors for Ocean Observation
abstract: As global environmental changes reshape the underwater biosphere, there is an increasing demand for more comprehensive and biologically relevant measurements to understand evolving conditions. Traditional aquatic measurements are often limited by static, coarse, sparse, and biased sampling methods. Animal-borne sensors offer a potential solution for monitoring marine animals and their physical environments in situ. However, invasive tagging can inevitably impact underwater movement. Here, we introduce a flexible and miniaturized electronic monitoring device designed for free-ranging animals. Our work focusses on the design of the sensing system, emphasizing its compact size, lightweight, flexibility, pressure-tolerance, and extended recording capabilities. The essential components, including sensors, flexible printed circuit boards, and waterproof encapsulation are strictly tested in high-pressure environments. The real-time data sampling is computed and processed on board to alleviate stress on the memory chip. By deploying these tags on animals worldwide, we can address critical data gaps, gain insights into changing ecosystems, and utilize them as active environmental sentinels.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis on Hydrodynamic Characteristics of Wing Stabilizers for Yachts
abstract: The wing stabilizer is a latest anti-rolling device for yachts which offers roll damping during cruising and zero speed. In this paper, we aim to investigate the lift/drag characteristics for the wing stabilizer by ANSYS. We focus on the impacts of aspect ratio on the lift/drag, so as to make reasonable suggestions on product development. Firstly, we create geometric models for wings in combination with the NACA0015 airfoil with the area 0.5m2 at different aspect ratios, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$AS = 1, 3, 5, 7$</tex>. Secondly, we investigate the effects of attack angles <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex>=10°, 15°, 20°, 30° and motion periods <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>=1s, 2s, 4s on hydrodynamic characteristics of stabilizers with different aspect ratios by using 3D dynamic mesh technique. Finally, for practical purposes, the aspect ratio is discussed based on the simulation results.

articleTitle: SeLT: Sonar Echo Image Recognition for Small Targets Using Lightweight Swin Transformer
abstract: Underwater sonar echo image data containing targets is relatively scarce, usually limiting the recognition performance of the model when employing a high-capacity (even state-of-the-art) network for recognition. To address this issue, we propose SeLT, a lightweight adaptation of the Swin-T,using lightweight feature extraction and feature coding modules. Specifically, we have reduced the stacking of Swin Transformer blocks and introduced a lightweight channel attention module to replace the MLP in each block. This eases the requirements for training data and computing resources, greatly accelerating the model training phase. Extensive experiments have demonstrated that, compared to the original Swin-T,our model achieves higher recognition performance (increasing 1.9% in terms of AUC value) with fewer parameters (reduced by 71%) and lower computational complexity (reduced by 73%).

articleTitle: Weakly-Supervised Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Hard Constraints for Sound Propagation Problems in Complex Environments *
abstract: Sound propagation problems in complex environments attract a great deal of interest. Traditional methods often rely on various approximations, coupled with difficulties in generalization. Therefore, this paper proposes the hard-constraint physics-informed neural networks model (hPINN) to solve partial differential equations (PDEs) by minimizing the loss function and incorporating boundary conditions into the network structure. Simulations have shown that the hard-constraint PINN can provide more consistent solutions to the wave equation compared to traditional methods without handling grid partitioning problems. After the weakly-supervised training, the hard-constraint PINN provides a better fitting at boundary values and is less prone to overfitting compared to the traditional soft-constraint PINN (soft-constraint PINN), which demostrates its efficiency.

articleTitle: Box-supervised Ocean Object Instance Segmentation Based on Object-BoxInst Network
abstract: Ocean data for instance segmentation is scarce and labeling is complex and time-consuming. A weakly supervised instance segmentation method using a ship dataset labelled only with bounding box annotations to achieve instance segmentation of ocean objects. We propose Object-BoxInst to improve ocean object instance segmentation performance without mask annotations. Object-BoxInst activates the object features in the box region of the class features and fuses them with the mask features to enhance the semantic information for mask prediction. Meanwhile, we build a Box Supervised Ocean Object InsSeg Dataset with 10,692 ship images and six classes. That has great significance to the application in the ocean field. The comparison experiment results show that Object-BoxInst has 40.21% AP, which is higher than BoxInst, thus effectively improving the ocean object accuracy of box-supervised segmentation.

articleTitle: Motion Simulation and Force Analysis of a CFD-based DP Vessel under Environmental Interference
abstract: In this study, based on computational fluid dynamics (CFD), the motion simulation of a dynamic positioning (DP) vessel model is carried out in view of the uncertainty of vessel motion. For the influence of external wave interference forces on vessel motion, a CFD method is proposed to simulate the change of a DP vessel's six degrees of freedom (6-DOF) motion, and the change rules of each degree of freedom under different wave angles are obtained. Aiming at the uncertainty of the DP vessel's motion resistance change at low speed under the sea conditions of level 3 ∼ 5, a prediction algorithm based on BP neural network is proposed to introduce into the scale model. At the same time, the influence and change of yaw angle and heave in this environment and the feasibility of scale model in simulation are studied. The simulation results validate the effectiveness of the prediction algorithm. The changing patterns and predictive data of vessel motion are helpful for DP vessel heading control and the design of pressure-type special materials. This study has important engineering and practical significance.

articleTitle: Energy Assessment of a Wave Energy Converter in Ustica Island. A Case Study
abstract: In the global energy scenario entered the sea generation for a few years ago. This includes the exploitation of sea and ocean masses for energy production. Governments are focusing on these technologies by encouraging incentives and action plans. This paper analyzes the current situation of wave technologies and describes a case study of power generation. A wave energy converter (WEC) was modeled located on the coast of Ustica, a small island located in Sicily, Italy. The hypothesized model and electrical energy producibility will be described.

articleTitle: Single-Photon LiDAR System Noise Modeling and Virtual Image Synthesis Technology for Sea Observation
abstract: Single-photon lidar has higher resolution, sensitivity, and immunity to interference compared with conventional lidar, and is suitable for low signal-to-noise ratio environments and applications that require high-precision target information. However, noise modeling of the information acquisition process of single-photon lidar systems has been a challenging problem that severely limits the performance of single-photon lidar systems in practical applications such as performance evaluation, design optimization, and prediction. In this way, we modeled the noise of single-photon lidar systems during underwater information acquisition by establishing a simple model of underwater noise, followed by using the model to generate an underwater dataset of single-photon lidar systems on the VOC2007 dataset. The evaluation indicator metrics indicate that the sea observation dataset has high fidelity. The established noise model and the synthesized dataset are of great help to single photon LiDAR system imaging, image enhancement, target detection, and other vision tasks.

articleTitle: Improved Underwater Transparent Organism Detection Based on YOLOv8
abstract: In order to improve the detection accuracy of underwater transparent organisms and solve the problems of missed detection or poor detection results of underwater trans-parent organisms. In terms of detection, an improved YOLOv8 algorithm is proposed for underwater transparent biological detection, which includes introducing Convolutional Block Attention Mechanism (CBAM) to build a backbone network, enhancing the perceptual ability of the convolutional neural network, and enhancing the feature extraction ability of the backbone network. Using the Focal loss function to alleviate class imbalance in the dataset; Add a small object detection head to YOLOv8 to detect relatively small underwater transparent targets, in order to improve the accuracy of object detection. The experimental results show that compared with the traditional YOLOv8 algorithm, the proposed algorithm improves mAP by 2.27%. The effectiveness and superiority of the improved YOLOv8 algorithm in this article have been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Electro-Mechanical WEC Stabilization for Onshore Wave Energy Exploitation
abstract: The energy generated from harnessing sea waves is considered as a potential solution to the energy needs of small islands. The fundamental problem with the energy produced by wave energy devices is the quality of the energy itself, as it is deeply influenced by the unpredictable conditions inherent to the wave motion. Indeed, the energy produced from a direct connection between the collector and the generator is profoundly variable in terms of voltage and frequency. This prevents its direct input into the grid, as the latter is characterized by fixed frequency and voltage. The objective of this paper is to demonstrate how it is possible to normalize such energy by an electro-mechanical stabilizer.

articleTitle: Integrated Navigation Based on HG-RNN and EKF for Autonomous Underwater Vehicle
abstract: The rapid attenuation of radio signals underwater makes the GPS unable to receive signals, and the accumulated errors of the navigation system will continue to dissipate without timely correction, affecting the accomplishment of other under-water missions. Based on the above problems, this paper proposes an integrated navigation method using a hybrid gated recurrent neural network (HG-RNN) position correction model(PCM) to assist the conventional navigation algorithm extended Kalman filter (EKF). First, GPS positions with low update frequency are uniformly applied to navigation position with high update rate based on an improved incremental smoothing and mapping (iSAM) method. The position correction model is then used to learn the relationship between the serial data from the navigation sensors and the positions of the improved iSAM algorithm. The GPS position is used as an observation when GPS is valid, otherwise, the position output from the position correction model is used as an observation. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can effectively improve the navigation accuracy.

articleTitle: A Novel Pickup Technique for Enhanced Sensitivity of Energy Harvesters and Vibration Sensors
abstract: This paper proposes a novel multi-capacitor signal pickup technique for vibration sensors/accelerometers and energy harvesters. In this structure, the sensitivity of the piezoelectric pickup in devices like accelerometers, energy harvesters, and pressure sensors can be significantly enhanced. The design is studied with TCAD simulation using COMSOL for a circular diaphragm MEMs having multi-capacitor sensing structure and is compared with conventional sensing/pick-up. To demonstrate the performance of the proposed technique, aluminum nitride (AIN) is used as a piezoelectric material. We show that the sensitivity of the accelerometer and the maximum power of the energy harvester, and hence power density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(mW/mm^{3})$</tex>, is enhanced by a factor of four or more. The proposed technique has a high potential for improving the performance of a variety of vibration pickup devices and MEM-based structures used in applications such as accelerometers, energy harvesters, and pressure sensors.

articleTitle: A Horizontal Spiral Motion Control Method Based on Marine Environmental Data for an Underwater Vehicle to Sample Deep-Sea Macrogenetic
abstract: The complex marine environment with high salinity, high pressure, low temperature, low nutrients, and absence of light, makes the ocean the largest ecosystem on earth, which still harbors microbial resources that remain largely unrecognized and untapped. Autonomous underwater vehicle equipped with deep-sea microbial sampler (AUV-MS) has currently become hotspot research for marine biologists to clarify the distribution of deep-sea microorganisms, which is closely related to dissolved oxygen, chlorophyll, temperature, light, and other factors in the marine environment. How to plan the voyage path of AUV-MS based on the information of oxygen, chlorophyll, temperature, etc., in the marine environment is the basis for realizing high-quality deep-sea microbial sampling. Therefore, a horizontal spiral motion and control method by adjusting the rudder angle and propeller speed of an AUV-MS is proposed, which is based on recognizing the distribution of chlorophyll in the environment.

articleTitle: Analyzing and Classifying Fish Vocalization in the East China Sea Coastal Area
abstract: This paper addresses the processing and classification of raw audio data collected from the coastal region of the East China Sea over a 24-hour period. The methodology involves preprocessing, feature extraction, feature selection, and classification. The raw signals undergo pre-emphasis and bandpass filtering, followed by segmentation techniques to identify individual fish vocalizations. The analysis of 72,324 segmented fish vocalization samples reveals two distinct types, Type A and Type B, constituting 74.60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and 25.40%, respectively. Feature extraction encompasses time, frequency, and cepstral domains. The random forest algorithm is employed for forward feature selection to reduce data dimensionality and eliminate redundant information. In the final stage, different classifiers are cascaded to enhance accuracy by mitigating potential misclassifications. The paper presents a focused and effective framework for the processing and classification of raw audio data, specifically targeting fish vocalizations in the coastal region of the East China Sea.

Author Keywords: coastal area of East China Sea

articleTitle: Data-Based Acoustic Far Scattered Field Prediction in Underwater Environment
abstract: The prediction of the scattered field of underwater targets is of significant importance for tasks such as target detection, recognition, and the active control of the scattered field. The Equivalent Source Method (ESM) stands out as a widely employed technique for reconstructing the field. ESM entails the synthesis of the acoustic field scattered from arbitrarily shaped targets by combining acoustic fields generated through virtual sources distributed on an equivalent source surface. In an environment with boundaries, estimating or simulating the transfer function is necessary, as seen in scenarios such as rooms or underwater environments. However, challenges arise in modeling the Green function using knowledge about environmental parameters due to mismatches between the model and actual conditions. Consequently, a data-based transfer function is often preferred over a modeled one. The conventional ray-based blind deconvolution (RBD) is constrained to estimating the amplitude-normalized Green function, leading to a loss of amplitude information. This paper introduces a blind deconvolution-based far-field prediction method that incorporates the estimation of the data-based transfer function. The contribution of this approach lies in estimating the Source Level (SL) based on RBD, facilitating accurate estimation of the amplitude of the transfer function. This method provides a practical means to predict the far scattered field of the target without depending on intricate details of environmental parameters.

articleTitle: uBlueTec - Training Framework on Underwater Tecs as Key Enabler for Blue Careers Development
abstract: While Blue Economy remains a fundamental sector in many world economies, its needs and impacts require specialized skills. For the sustainability of blue economy sectors, both technical skills (blue and digital) and green skills are needed. Identifying a skills gap, the uBlueTec project aims to set up, test and validate a triple transition training and skills development model (green, blue, digital skills). Through a durable partnerships among universities, VET providers, clusters and Small and Medium Entreprises (SMEs), the project will developed curricula and implement pilots both for VET and Higher Education levels. The article describes the skills gaps analysis and preliminary work on the curricula.

articleTitle: Multipath Propagation Characteristics of Line-Spectrum Noise Radiated by Underwater Targets Under a Fluctuating Sea Surface
abstract: Most of the existing underwater target depth estimation methods rely on matched field or matched normal mode processing, which require precise in-site parameters or accurate separation and identification of the normal modes, thus increasing method complexity. In the actual ocean waveguide, the sea surface often undergoes dynamic fluctuations due to environmental factors such as sea wind. The reflection effect of the sea surface causes the multipath propagation of the line-spectrum noise radiated by the underwater targets. Meanwhile, the scattering effect of the dynamically fluctuating sea surface leads to the undulating propagation of the line-spectrum noise. Numerical simulation results demonstrate that the dynamically fluctuating sea surface exhibits varying amplitude modulation effects for different ray arrival paths. Moreover, for the line-spectrum noise propagating along the same ray arrivals, distinct modulation effects are observed for different source depths. The above phenomenon provides potential method for addressing the target depth estimation problems based on the amplitude differences of the modulation effects for different ray arrivals.

articleTitle: An Efficient Signal and Noise Simulator for Imaging Sonar
abstract: High-frequency imaging sonar systems are a critical technology for underwater sensing. Design and experimental validation of signal processing algorithms for image reconstruction is very challenging due to difficulties in deployment and accurate positioning. Modelling and simulation are powerful tools to evaluate the system before prototyping. Unfortunately, there are only a few simulation tools available, and the computation complexity for accurate simulation is very high. Most of the simulators directly convert the estimated target range, receive beam direction and reflected intensity level in to synthetic sonar image. These simulators are not accounting for the spatial response of the array with beamformer and temporal response of the waveform, while generating the image. To evaluate the effectiveness of different signal processing techniques for image reconstruction, a received signal model for the sensor array considering the array and waveform properties is essential. This paper presents an efficient signal and noise simulator, to generate the sonar receiver array signal time series for practical imaging scenarios, with five times lesser computation time compared to the state-of-the-art simulator reported in the literature. The simulator also contains a basic sonar processing module which performs near-field beamforming, matched filtering and image processing on the simulated signal, to generate the final sonar image. Optimisation in the sonar receiver and signal processing can be conveniently evaluated through this simulation scheme. The simulation results are compared with experimental results to verify the simulation model. Being generic in nature this simulator can simulate sector scan sonar, single beam and multi-beam side scan sonars simultaneously for the same simulation scenario. This enables verification of co-registration of side scan and gap filler sonar images.

articleTitle: A Link Quality-Aware Adaptive MAC Protocol Based on Clustering for Underwater Acoustic Network
abstract: The Medium Access Control (MAC) protocols have a significant impact on the performance of underwater acoustic sensor networks. However, the design of the MAC protocol has faced many challenges, such as application in clustering routing and link interruptions caused by uncertainty of underwater acoustic channels. A link quality-aware adaptive MAC protocol (LQAA-MAC) based on cluster is proposed to address the two challenges. LQAA-MAC is based on the scheduling scheme, it can adaptively adjust the backoff mechanism according to the quality of the channel and calculated collision probability in the cluster. Simulation results show the LQAA-MAC achieves a high packet delivery ratio and improves the network throughput while ensuring end-to-end delay.

articleTitle: Dual Use of High Frequency Radar for Ocean Remote Sensing and High-Speed Target Detection
abstract: High frequency (HF) radar has been widely used for ocean surface dynamics remote sensing, including the current, wave, and wind parameters, as well as vessel detection and tracking. Besides, it is also an important tool for aircraft surveillance, particularly the flying stealth targets. Unlike the vessel targets, aircraft are characterized by high-speed motion, which produces more serious range and Doppler migration. Hence, it is challenging to simultaneously detect the slow- and high-speed targets under the same radar waveform configuration. In this paper, a long-time coherent integration method based on the generalized Radon-Fourier transform (GRFT) is applied to deal with this problem. To further address the effect of the target's signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) fluctuation, a non-coherent integration based amplitude fluctuation suppression (AFS) method is proposed to refine GRFT's result. Preliminary experimental results prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Unmanned Vehicles: A Promising Solution to Addressing Sea Pollution
abstract: Monitoring and controlling maritime pollution is critical, especially in countries with a vast Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). The CleanSeaNet satellite monitoring system, developed and implemented by the European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA), plays a crucial role in the surveillance of potential hydrocarbons and hazardous substances spills in the ocean. When a potential oil spill is detected, the respective coastal state is alerted, allowing them to take the necessary operational and legal measures. The use of unmanned vehicles (aerial and surface) presents a promising solution to address sea pollution to reduce operational costs and improve response capabilities. The vast evolution in the field of unmanned vehicles allows easier integration and implementation of a network at a national level. A national network of unmanned vehicles can also be applied in other domains, such as surveillance in fire-prone areas of high risk. The analysis carried out shows that a national network of unmanned vehicles is a promising solution to address sea pollution.

articleTitle: The feasibility assessment of zero-meter isobaths localization using the UNet architecture
abstract: Coastal erosion has a profound impact on coastal cities. Consequently, closely monitoring trends in coastal changes is essential. Recognizing the prevalent complexity and high costs associated with existing measurement methods, this study integrates state-of-the-art artificial intelligence technologies to propose an economical and efficient approach for understanding coastal morphology change. The research findings confirm the practicality and feasibility of the proposed methodology, emphasizing its potential significance in addressing coastal erosion challenges.

articleTitle: Estimation of Time-Varying Underwater Acoustic Channel Via Dynamic Proximal Gradient Algorithm
abstract: Dynamic compressed sensing (DCS) techniques have been applied to enhance the performance of channel estimation (CE) in underwater acoustic (UWA) communications. Existing DCS-CE schemes are mainly applicable to slow-varying channels and solutions working under rapid channel conditions are highly desirable. In this paper, tracking of time-varying sparse UWA channel is formulated as a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell_{p}$</tex> -norm regularized recursive least square (RLS) problem, which is then solved via a proximal gradient (PG) algorithm. The resulting CE scheme is named the dynamic PG (DPG) CE method. Experimental results verified the advantage of the proposed DPG CE scheme over existing sparse CE schemes.

articleTitle: Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition Method Based on Physical Information Driving Frequency Attention
abstract: In passive Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition (UATR) task, ship radiated noise comprises low-frequency line spectrum, which contains the physical information of ship radiated noise characteristics. A UATR method based on Physical Information driving Frequency Attention (PI _ FA) is proposed. In the first step of PI _ FA, the deep features in each frequency are encoded to physical information parameters. Then, the parameters express the harmonic of low-frequency line spectrum with help of a specifically designed activation function. Therefore, the PI _ FA can help the deep recognition model focus on the harmonic of low-frequency line spectrum and learn line spectrum features. In this paper, an ablation experiment and a feature visualization experiment are designed to verify the validity of the PI _ F A. The ablation experiment results show that PI_ FA achieve 0.92%-6.31 % better than other Attention in recognition accuracy. The feature visualization experiment results verify that PI _F A can effectively focus on the harmonic of low-frequency line spectrum in ship radiated noise. Visualization experimental results show t feature maps can learn of the harmonic of low-frequency line spectrum features with driven by physical information via PI _ FA. The experimental results show that PI _ FA can achieve better recognition performance in task of UATR.

articleTitle: Study on the Influence of the Towing Parameters Variations on the Towing Depth
abstract: Underwater towing systems play an important role in ocean exploration, many ocean observatory activities rely on them. High speed deep sea towing systems can explore deep sea at a very fast speed. Achieving fast speed in the deep sea is a difficult task, it lacks correlational theory. To achieve this, towing parameters need more reasonable values. For example, cables must have small drag coefficient, otherwise a very long cable is needed. To illustrate the influence of the towing parameters variations on the towing depth, a cable-towed body and hydrofoil model using the lumped mass method is built. Towing depths are calculated by the model when towing parameters change. By analyzing the results, extent of the influence of different parameters on the towing depth is evaluated. The result has enlightenment effect on the depth control of high speed deep sea towing systems.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Water Exit of Two-Dimensional Hydrofoil
abstract: In this paper, the hydrodynamic characteristics of the hydrofoil during water exit are investigated numerically. The interaction between hydrofoil wake vortex and free surface is studied under different conditions. Furthermore, the influence of angle of attack and water-exit angle of hydrofoil are analyzed and evaluated. The results show that the deformation of the free surface caused by water-exit of the hydrofoil is consistent with that of the hydrofoil wake vortex. Besides, the hydrofoil produces obvious force oscillation in the process of water exit, and the amplitude of oscillation is related to the angle of attack and water-exit angle.

articleTitle: Marine Seismic P-Phase Picking Network for Floating Seismographs Using Transfer Learning
abstract: P-phase picking is especially crucial in marine earthquake because the P-wave is the first-arrival wave, which can be used for early warning and seafloor geological imaging. However, due to the scarcity of data, the performance of P-phase picking in marine earthquake is not satisfactory, especially in floating seismographs. In this paper, we use land seismic data to guide floating seismographs data, propose a transfer-learned method for P-phase picking in marine earthquake, and propose a ID axial attention module, significantly improving the performance of marine seismic P-phase picking under limited data. Experimental results show that our model has a higher Fl-score of 97.4% compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Mooring Optimal Heading Control Based on Finite-time Convergent Disturbance Observer for FPSO with Structural Reliability and Thruster Assistance
abstract: A novel mooring heading control strategy for FPSO vessels is proposed to tackle the complex and dynamic harsh marine environment. The strategy incorporates a safe and energy-efficient thruster-assisted mooring control system. Initially, a finite-time convergent disturbance observer (FCDO) is used for the online estimation of unknown time-varying disturbances. After that, an optimal heading direction algorithm based on the mooring cable tension is proposed to calculate the expected heading direction in order to reduce the influence of environmental interference and reduce energy consumption. By integrating disturbance estimation and optimal heading design, the finite-time convergent disturbance observer reliability-based dynamic surface (FCDORD) controller is enhanced with a structural reliability index. This allow for the development of a safe and energy-efficient thruster-assisted mooring control system. Extensive stability analysis demonstrates that all errors are constrained within acceptable limits, and a series of simulations confirms the reliability, safety, and energy efficiency of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Doppler Frequency Components Separation from Range-Doppler Spectrum Using Shipboard Coherent Microwave Radar
abstract: Shipboard coherent microwave radar is becoming an emerging tool for wave detection. However, the ship's motion and broken waves would introduce extra Doppler components into the Doppler spectrum of the sea echo. On the one hand, the direct relation between the orbital velocity of gravity waves and the wave height spectrum is used for wave parameters inversion in coherent microwave radar. On the other hand, in the study of the evolution of air-sea exchange in which ocean waves and kinetic energy break into each other, the Doppler frequency components generated by Bragg scattering from bro-ken short waves need to be extracted for analysis. Separating each frequency component in the Doppler spectrum is of great significance in improving wave characteristics investigation and wave detection performance using shipboard coherent microwave radar. To address this issue, a method that uses the objective function maximization to fit the Doppler spectrum is illustrated. To validate the proposed method, the experimental data collected with a shipboard S-band radar in the South China Sea in December 2020 was analyzed. The results indicate that the proposed method is effective for the separation of the frequency components. The proposed method in this paper also provides a possibility for studying the improvement of the accuracy of wave parameters inversion in shipboard coherent microwave radar and the evolution of air-sea exchange in which the energy and kinetic energy of wave breaking are exchanged.

articleTitle: A Novel Off-Grid DOA Estimation Approach Using Sparse Bayesian Learning
abstract: Sparse signal reconstruction methods for direction of arrival (DOA) estimation, such as sparse Bayesian learning (SBL), face the challenge of grid mismatch. Several off-grid DOA estimation methods have been proposed, but their performance depends on the tradeoff between accuracy and computational workload. In order to enhance the efficiency and performance of off-grid DOA estimation, we propose a grid refinement off-grid method based on sparse Bayesian learning (GROGSBL). We improve the stability of the grid refinement process by incorporating the off-grid model. Additionally, an off-grid DOA extraction method is adopted to further improve the accuracy of estimation. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances DOA estimation performance and exhibits superior computational efficiency.

articleTitle: A Key Agreement Algorithm for Securing Underwater Acoustic Communications
abstract: With the introduction of standards in underwater acoustic communications, protecting the content of packets sent underwater has become a pressing need. Since underwater devices can be compromised over long-term deployments, navies are reluctant to use encryption devices on the one hand; and on the other hand, they require secure communication without the use of pre-agreed secret keys for flexibility. To answer this demand, here we present a key agreement protocol to generate secret keys from the channel impulse response (CIR) between Alice and Bob. Considering the time-varying nature of the underwater acoustic CIR, our key generator is based on the parameters of the distribution of the random features that characterize the CIR rather than directly on the features themselves. Assuming CIR reciprocity, we estimate the CIR by transmitting probe signals between Alice and Bob, and synchronize the probe transmissions such that signals fly by each other while still respecting the half-duplex constraints of underwater acoustic modems. In turn, Alice and Bob's packets arriving to Eve, the attacker, expose different CIRs and possibly collide. Modeled simulation results show agreement between the keys generated by Alice and Bob, and a significant difference with respect to the keys obtained by Eve.

articleTitle: A Variable Wingspan Scroll Telescopic Wing for Multimodal Underwater Vehicles
abstract: This paper presents the design of a variable wingspan scroll telescopic wing for multimodal underwater vehicles, enabling the vehicles to adjust their wingspans as needed for optimal maneuverability. Detailed descriptions of the mechanical structure, geometric relationships, and force analysis of the scroll telescopic wing are provided. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations are employed to obtain the hydrodynamic parameters of the multimodal underwater vehicles at different wingspans. Based on steady-state gliding analysis, the gliding characteristics of the vehicles at various wingspans are determined, further leading to the proposal of the wingspan adjustment strategy for the telescopic wing. Preliminary water tank experiments validate the feasibility of the variable wingspan scroll telescopic wing structure and the gliding characteristics of the vehicle at different wingspans.

articleTitle: Addressing the climate crisis on the coastal ecosystem using the Agenda 2030
abstract: The coastal zone includes a large share of the economic activity and the social development while the last years is getting even more vulnerable to climate crisis. Sea level rise and coastal erosion are the major threats of climate crisis to the coastal ecosystems. Among the multiple impacts of the sea level rise is the destruction of arable land and urban settlements, the displacement of marine and freshwater species, and the loss of coastal habitats. Climate crisis on the coastal zone can affect important sectors, like coastal property and infrastructure, coastal ecosystems and lead to land loss. Drivers from anthropogenic activities, such us the industrial development and tourism, act significant pressures to the coastal environment. Coastal ecosystems are crucial for the economy in regional, national, and international level. The adoption of a sustainable blue economy framework in the coastal zone is required for the protection of the coastal ecosystem from climate change. At the same time, the Agenda 2030 is characterized as the final call to stop the irreversible damage to the planet. With the extreme natural hazards and weather conditions, climate crisis underlines its presence, while the goals of the Agenda 2030 are more topical than ever. Under this scheme, a major challenge is the assessment of the Sustainable Development Goals regarding their importance for a sustainable blue economy in the coastal ecosystems. This study presents an approach for the analysis and the prioritization of the SDGs for the sustainable blue economy in a coastal industrialized ecosystem. The analysis of the SDGs is conducted in correspondence with the ecosystem services provided by the coastal industrialized ecosystem. Outcome of this approach is a decision-making tool that classifies the SDGs with a corresponding factor, according to their importance for the sustainable blue economy of the coastal ecosystem. Through the application of this approach, stakeholders can obtain information on which SDGs they should focus on and helping them prioritize their actions toward the achievement of a sustainable blue economy in the coastal ecosystem. Case study of this research is a coastal ecosystem in Athens metropolitan area (Greece), that includes intense industrial activity, important cultural heritage and a protected wetland. The application of this approach in the study area, indicates that 5 SDGs have a leading role to the achievement of sustainability in the coastal zone, while their accomplishment will improve the services and the goods provided by this ecosystem to the society.

articleTitle: DVL Calibration Using Data-Driven Methods
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are used in a wide range of underwater applications, ranging from seafloor mapping to industrial operations. While underwater, the AUV navigation solution commonly relies on the fusion between inertial sensors and Doppler velocity logs (DVL). To achieve accurate DVL measurements a calibration procedure should be conducted before the mission begins. Model-based calibration approaches include filtering approaches utilizing global navigation satellite system signals. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end deep-learning framework for the calibration procedure. Using stimulative data, we show that our proposed approach outperforms model-based approaches by 35% in accuracy and 80% in the required calibration time.

articleTitle: Concept of an autonomous in-situ sensor system for monitoring object movements caused by sea swells
abstract: The concept of an autonomous in-situ sensor system, Motion Probe, for monitoring wave induced motions of underwater objects is presented. This cost-effective system integrates a pressure sensor alongside inertial and optionally global positioning sensors to collect data on the seastate, as well as the movement, acceleration, and orientation of the designated test object. Energy-efficient features, wireless charging, and Wi-Fi data transmission enhance user-friendly operation. An innovative housing design is introduced to protect the sensor from external influences, ensuring its reliability in marine environments. The paper outlines the electronic implementation, energy management, and pressure housing design, emphasizing the Motion Probe’s potential for various research applications. Testing phases include functional tests under controlled laboratory environments and long term sea trials, providing insights into wave inducted object dynamics.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of the Magneto-Electro-Elastic Structures Using the Overlapping Finite Element Method
abstract: Due to the remarkable magneto-electro-elastic (MEE) coupling effects, the MEE materials have great potentials in the design of various hydrophones which are very important equipment in ocean engineering fields. To develop practical MEE-based devices efficiently, the finite element method (FEM) is always applied for the simulation of MEE structures. However, the strong reliability of the computation accuracy on the mesh qualities limits the efficiency of the FEM. The overlapping finite element method (OFEM) is characterized by ultra-accuracy and distortion insensitivity, so we establish the OFEM model for the MEE structures to predict the dynamic response of MEE devices. In our constructed OFEM model, the harmonic trigonometric functions are introduced as basis functions to mimic local behaviors of the MEE structures. A typical free vibration problem for MEE solids is considered in this work to evaluate the performance of OFEM. By comparing the numerical results from the OFEM and the FEM, it is examined that the OFEM is a very efficient approach for modelling MEE structures, with higher precision and distortion insensitivity than the FEM.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Multibeam Echosounder Bathymetry and Backscatter
abstract: Multibeam echosounders (MBES) are the tool of choice for high-precision underwater surveys, especially when water conditions render optical imagery ineffective. We present and evaluate the following approaches for MBES segmentation: (1) real-time processing of single sounding profiles using traditional machine learning techniques, (2) batch processing of “waterfall” pseudo-images using a standard U-Net model, (3) the same model adapted to 2D projections of 3D point clouds, and (4) post-mission, survey-level processing using modern networks specifically designed for sparse point clouds. Strengths and weaknesses of the methods are discussed, including data preprocessing requirements, robustness, and ease of implementation/interpretation. Evaluation is performed on real data collected by an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) during a deep-sea industrial pipeline inspection.

articleTitle: Understanding AUV Formations Through Fluid Dynamics: Strategies for Enhanced Energetic Efficiency
abstract: Much like how birds or fish move in specific formations to save energy, there is an opportunity for AUVs to adopt similar formations to maximize their energy efficiency. Such practices could revolutionize how we use AUVs for various oceanic activities in the future. In this study, to tackle the complex hydrodynamics in grouped AUVs, a two-tiered computational method is employed, encompassing both individual AUV analysis and collective behavior. We find that the most energy-efficient formations for AUV group, ranging from pairs to tens of individuals, is when one AUV trails to the side of another, and eventually results in a “chain” pattern optimal formation for large AUV group. Beyond the optimal chain formation, we investigated the fluid dynamics effects of specific typical formations such as wedge, line, diagonal line, rectangular and spiral shapes. These were then compared to the energy consumption of the optimal formation. These quantitative analyses may provide important reference in future marine exploration based on AUV groups.

articleTitle: Experimental Application of FMCW AoPCB Radar Technology in Support of Maritime Autonomous Docking
abstract: Recent investment into autonomous driving [1] has resulted in a multitude of technical advancements for mobile autonomous systems. Of particular note for maritime applications are improvements in sensing modalities, particularly radar sensors. Historically, maritime use has heavily relied on traditional radar sensing systems. These units are large, expensive, heavy, and require significant power to operate [2] [3]. In this paper we explore applying automotive-derived low cost, PCB mounted radar for autonomous maritime sensing applications. Our research indicates that these sensors perform effectively in cluttered maritime environments and are able to detect targets of interest such as docks, pilings, buoys, and other vessels. Integrating these sensors onto autonomous marine platforms is also feasible. We present both raw point cloud data displaying these objects from our field testing as well as the results of a software processing algorithm to identify such obstacles from radar sensor data.

articleTitle: Estimating Target Depth for Deep-Sea Active Sonars Through Channel-Impulse-Response Matching
abstract: Target depth estimation in deep sea is an important topic in underwater acoustic signal processing. In recent years, researchers [1]–[3] proposed some methods of estimating depth of underwater sources for passive acoustic systems with vertical line arrays. These vertical arrays are located at great depth at the point where the sound speed equals the maximum speed near the surface, which makes use of the deep-sea propagation characteristics of reliable acoustic path. However, using active sonars located at the great depth to estimate near-surface target depth has rarely been investigated. This paper focuses on target depth estimation of active sonars with a single hydrophone or horizontal line array at the great depth.

articleTitle: Underwater Vortex Source Localization Using an Artificial Lateral Line System with Differential Pressure and Velocity Sensors
abstract: Fish can sense the surrounding hydrodynamic stimuli for obstacle recognition and wake tracking with the lateral line system, which has inspired many studies of artificial lateral line systems (ALLS). Here, we propose a fusion sensing modality of differential pressure and velocity for ALLS to localize underwater vortex sources. This ALLS employs a sensor layout strategy based on maximization hydrodynamic stimuli. Dual-modal fusion sensing significantly reduces the vortex source localization error over the single-modal sensing approach due to the anisotropic response properties of the differential pressure and flow velocity sensors to the downstream and lateral distances of the vortex source. Experiments show that in the range of 1 body length (BL), the mean localization error of the vortex source is about 0.11BL. The proposed dual-sensing fusion approach provides new insight into the application of vortex source localization for underwater vehicles.

articleTitle: Development of Broadband Underwater Transducers and Arrays
abstract: This paper describes the development of broadband underwater (U/W) transducers at Microfine Materials Technologies Pte Ltd, Singapore. A range of low-to-mid frequency (10–40 kHz) broadband U/W transducers of Tonpilz (TP) designs are available, including single crystal motor sections of spoke-like and square-pipe constructions and cost-effective versions driven by piezoceramic rings. Also available are new transmission-line (TL) design of acoustically-matched transmitter element of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<<\lambda_{\mathrm{w}}/2$</tex> in head mass diameter, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\mathrm{w}}$</tex> being the wavelength in water at the operating central frequency. High-elemental density low-frequency arrays are possible with the new TL design. Together with high-frequency piezocomposite transmitter array, which is embedded among the small footprint TL elements, slim transmitter arrays for dual-/ triple-frequency synthetic aperture sonar (SAS) applications are now possible. Also described are other high-performance devices including miniature high-sensitivity hydrophones and vector sensors, as well as cost effective piezoceramic-based broadband 31-mode free flooded ring transducers of a few kHz in central frequency.

articleTitle: On the Importance of Domain Knowledge for Real-Time Event Detection
abstract: Due to the complexity and dynamics of marine ecosystems, real-time monitoring and possibilities for anticipatory intervention are required. This study emphasises the crucial role of domain (expert) knowledge in developing effective realtime event detection systems. Focusing on the Change Event based Sensor Sampling (ChESS) project, which utilises methods based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) for the analysis of marine data streams, the research integrates stakeholder input and domain knowledge into the development process. Using data from the Time-Series Station (TSS) Spiekeroog, domain knowledge influences the design of software architecture, algorithms, goals and constraints, data retrieval, and related actions as an automated triggering of a water sampler. Lessons learned stress the importance of early domain expert involvement and highlight the value of combining technological advancements with domain insights. Participatory approaches enhance the development of monitoring systems, supporting informed decision-making for sustainable marine ecosystem management.

articleTitle: Adaptive Target Track Fusion Based on Track Quality Assessment for T/R - R Composite Compact HFSWR
abstract: Compact high-frequency surface wave radar (HF-SWR) suffers from a low azimuth accuracy for target detection, leading to a low target positioning accuracy. Either monostatic T/R radar or bistatic T-R radar is difficult to accurately estimate the target kinematic parameters. To resolve this problem, an adaptive track fusion method based on track quality assessment is proposed in this paper. First, two indexes are proposed according to the vessel motion characteristics to evaluate the overall track quality in terms of uncertainty and smoothness. Subsequently, the two indexes are integrated to produce fusion weights for the target range and azimuth, respectively. The obtained weights are used to weight the range and azimuth data sequences measured by two radars to obtain a preliminary fused track. Next, the instantaneous course data sequences for the preliminary fused track and two radar tracks are separately estimated, and the course difference data sequences between the preliminary fused track and each radar track are obtained. Then a dynamic weight data sequence is calculated using the course difference data sequence.
