Finally, the obtained dynamic weights are used to weigh the range and azimuth data sequences of two radar tracks to produce the final fused track. Experiment results with both simulated and field data demonstrate that the proposed method improves the target positioning accuracy significantly.

articleTitle: Performance Estimation of Parameter Fusion Strategies for Improved Seafloor Classification for Mn-Crust Survey using AUV Data
abstract: This paper compares the performance of seafloor classification methods based on data collected by autonomous robotic surveys of Cobalt-rich Manganese Crust deposits. Parameters were extracted from acoustic subbottom data using an autoencoder automatically, whereas visual data in the form of 3D color point clouds were analyzed to calculate physical parameters using mathematical equations. SVM classifiers were trained for each sensor modality, which showed that the acoustic classifier performed better than visual classifier. Middle fusion method, in which both parameter vectors are combined into a unified feature vector, performed better on almost every measure of performance than the previous two. Furthermore, it could prevent misclassification from both modalities.

articleTitle: A TDOA Method for Underwater Target Location Based on Particle Swarm Optimization with Experiment Verification
abstract: TDOA methods play a significant role in passive target location. When using the time difference of arrival (TDOA) method to passively locate underwater targets, measurement errors can inevitably affect the accuracy of the location. This paper proposes a TDOA method based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) for locating underwater targets using distributed multi-agent systems. The simulation results demonstrate the method's effectiveness. An experiment was conducted to verify the method at sea in Sanya Bay in the South China Sea. The method's performance was verified at sea, demonstrating an average location error of 7.41 m. Compared to TDOA-Taylor, the method exhibits a 9.74% reduction in location error.

articleTitle: Ship Open Set Recognition Based on Auditory Deep CNN
abstract: In practical engineering application, ship targets recognition must face the problem of Open Set Recognition (OSR). For ship targets OSR problem, the paper presents a new method. Inspired by the auditory perception mechanism, the proposed method builds the auditory deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and uses the auditory deep CNN to extract the auditory deep features of the training set to build feature template, and matches the template with the auditory deep features of the test set samples. Finally, the ship radiated noise open set recognition of is completed by designing the template matched threshold. The experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively realize the open set recognition of ship targets.

articleTitle: Fractional Fourier Transform Based Channel Estimation in Underwater Acoustic Communications
abstract: Underwater communications have severe channel distortions which can greatly affect its performance. This paper proposes a novel approach for estimating channel parameters (multipath delay and Doppler scaling) for underwater acoustic channels. The method is a Fractional Fourier Transform (FrFT) based approach with linear frequency-modulated (chirp) signals as a pilot. Innovation lies in the receiver design, where a 2D array is formed by performing a scan of FrFTs on the received signal. Key point detection algorithms are exploited to extract distinct X-shaped features in a 2D array, allowing for simultaneous estimation of both channel delay and Doppler parameters for all multipath components. The novel approach avoids the costly iterative process used in existing algorithms, which calculates Doppler scaling for one path per iteration. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is capable of estimating channel parameters in a severely time-delayed and Doppler-scaled multipath channel. The algorithm achieved a ±0.1% estimation accuracy with Doppler scaling factors ranging between 0.95 to 1.05. Multipath delay was estimated to within ±2ms for delays ranging from 0 to 0.2 seconds.

articleTitle: Global Significant Wave Height Retrieval from Spaceborne GNSS-R Using Transformers
abstract: Global significant wave height (SWH) is a crucial element in ocean observation and spaceborne global navigation satellite system reflectometry (GNSS-R) stands as a novel remote sensing technique to achieve large-scale measurement. Delay Doppler Map (DDM) is a basic observable of GNSS-R and existing studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in SWH retrieval from DDMs. However, CNNs are constrained by their limited receptive field, lacking the capability to establish long-range dependencies for the entire DDMs. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel model called WaveFormer which utilizes transformer architecture to extract features from DDMs. To evaluate the performance of the developed method, experiments are conducted on Cyclone GNSS (CYGNSS) data and results illustrate that WaveFormer achieves a lower root mean square deviation (RMSD) of 0.452 m than the CNN-based method.

articleTitle: Sail-rudder Collaborative Control of Unmanned Sailboat Based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Unmanned sailboats have gained a lot of interest in recent years due to their low energy consumption and long endurance, which has great potential in obtaining sea surface meteorological information. It is challenging to perform effective control due to their strongly nonlinear and coupling characteristics. This work develops a sail-rudder collaborative control method for an unmanned sailboat based on reinforcement learning using Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient. The kinematic model of a 12-foot sailboat and the model of time-varying wind and ocean current are employed in Matlab software to train the control policy. A series of simulations are conducted and the results verify the effectiveness of the control policy.

articleTitle: Predictive Disturbance Rejection Method to Control Vessels in Presence of Currents and Wind
abstract: In this paper, a methodology to incorporate esti-mates of predicted disturbances into model predictive trajec-tory tracking controllers is described. Model predictive control (MPC) is a widely used control technique which allows to calculate actual control moves based on modelled future behavior. Commonly, MPC uses estimates of effective disturbances in order to reject these by counteracting them. This work extends standard approaches by assuming that disturbances are not constant over the entire prediction horizon but instead can change. With this, forecasts of upcoming disturbances along the trajectory can be integrated as additional input vector into the optimization problem. This approach is then exemplarily tested for vessels in currents, but can be applied to all types of vehicles and disturbances. Since solving the optimization problem becomes computationally expensive and disturbances often cannot be modelled as an analytical function of space and time, computations of the disturbance vector are brought forward under strict assumptions. Finally, the algorithm is simulatively tested and compared against a standard disturbance rejection approach to underline its benefits.

articleTitle: SOUND: A Swarm of Low-Cost Floaters for Sustainable Fishing
abstract: The SOUND project focuses on developing a swarm of low-cost Lagrangian floaters capable of providing non-invasive aquaculture and fishing support, especially in remote areas and developing countries. The floaters drift with the current and use their buoyancy control mechanism to achieve profiling and depth-keeping behaviours, performing active acoustic fish detection and biomass assessment. This paper details the mechanical and algorithmic design of the SOUND floater prototype, as well as results achieved in laboratory experiments and during sea trials.

articleTitle: Study of SNR Improvement of an Equivalent Pressure Signal Obtained from an Inertial Type Acoustic Vector Sensor
abstract: An inertial type Acoustic Vector Sensor (AVS) measures 4D sound field information through pressure and acceleration signals along three orthogonal axes using an omnidirectional hydrophone and a tri-axial accelerometer sensor. Its features, such as its compact size, intrinsic directionality, and frequency-independent beam pattern, make it more attractive than conventional pressure hydrophone arrays for various applications. However, the impact of noise may still restrict its applicability for detecting weak signals, especially in low SNR scenarios. We have investigated a signal processing technique combining signals from all channels of the AVS to obtain a pressure-equivalent signal with a higher SNR than the omnidirectional hydrophone. This combined signal corresponds to a beam-steered output with a cardioid beam pattern. The performance is assessed in terms of the Array Gain (AG), which measures the improvement in SNR of the combined signal compared to the SNR achieved from the pressure signal alone. In an isotropic noise background, AVS theoretically provides an AG of 3–6 dB. In this paper, we have analyzed the different combinations of the AVS channels and obtained their combined AG. The effect of the weights selected for combining the different channels of the AVS is also reported. Further, the simulation study findings are corroborated with field experiment data collected using a custom-built AVS. The results and inferences from simulated and field data are discussed and presented.

articleTitle: Adaptive Detection Method for Dual Threshold Broadband Underwater Acoustic Signals Based on Morphological Filtering
abstract: The passive detection of underwater acoustic signals is susceptible to the self-noise of the sensor platform and the nonstationary ocean environmental noise, resulting in high rates of false alarms and missed detections using conventional signal detection methods. To address the above issues, this paper applies morphological filtering to the frequency domain power spectrum for morphology correction, and uses dual thresholds: the noise threshold and the rising and falling edge threshold detection for broadband signal detection, obtaining superior results compared to the traditional detection methods. In the 2023 South China Sea Experiment, a single-channel hydrophone was mounted on an underwater glider to collect acoustic data. The analysis of the experimental data has validated the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Modelling of Underwater Target for Sector Scan Sonar Imaging using K-Wave Toolbox
abstract: Underwater acoustic imaging is fast growing as an inevitable underwater imaging modality due to the ability of the same to image turbid sea bottoms. Sector scan and side-looking sonars (SLS) yield essentially identical acoustic images by projecting a sound beam at a shallow angle towards the seafloor. The sector-scan sonar typically employs a display known as a plan position indicator (PPI), which essentially represents a segment of a polar coordinate plot. In this study, we propose an efficient sector scan sonar imaging technique for modelling underwater targets using the k-Wave toolbox. k-Wave has the benefit of modelling the 3D environment with the ability to assign the sound speed and medium density at the voxel level, providing more accurate backscattered echoes for various sonar signal processing applications. It also has the advantage of offering precise and computationally effective simulation for acoustic imaging.

articleTitle: Design and development of an observational network and associated technologies for subsea carbon sequestration site assessments
abstract: Marine monitoring and Verification (MM&V) in support of marine carbon capture and storage projects (CCS) can present a lot of challenges for operators and regulators. In supporting the assessment of a potential marine CCS site in Gippsland, the CSIRO developed a multi-modal monitoring plan to better understand site conditions and inform the natural background variability present at the location of interest.

articleTitle: Matching-Pursuit Based Adaptive Turbo Equalization Algorithm for Underwater Acoustic Channels
abstract: Adaptive turbo equalization (ATEQ) based on the normalized minimum symbol error rate (NMSER) criterion demonstrates powerful detection performance in underwater acoustic (UWA) communications. However, the long delay spreads of the UWA channels usually lead to very high-order channel equalizers, and result in very slow convergence with massive turbo iterations with ATEQ. In this paper, we design a matching-pursuit based ATEQ (MP-ATEQ) algorithm. MP-ATEQ is based on NMSER criterion and updates the taps of the equalizers in the matching-pursuit manner. It leverages the sparse nature of the UWA channels to improve channel equalization, and can lead to a lower BER without initial settings of the taps. And the MP-TEQ can work with block-wise updates, therefore can easily deal with the high-order equalizers with only a few turbo iterations. Simulation and experimental results show that the proposed MP-TEQ outperforms other NMSER-based algorithms in UWA channels without additional complexity cost.

articleTitle: Development of an Energy-Efficient Control System for Underwater Gliders
abstract: In underwater gliders, certain inefficiencies in energy supply strategies and control methods, such as imbalanced energy distribution, lead to the control system consuming an estimated 95% of the total energy budget, indicating a critical need for optimization in these areas. This study assesses the specific impacts of energy supply strategies and control methods on the efficiency and performance of underwater gliders, focusing on optimizing the control system for low-power consumption. Firstly, guided by the working principles and operational procedures of underwater gliders, a single-profile energy consumption model for the control system was established, which facilitates accurate energy usage tracking and management, contributing to the identification of potential efficiency improvements. Secondly, following a meticulous examination of the power supply voltage requirements for each component within the control system, a multi-supply and multi-voltage (MSMV) scheme was designed. This scheme, in conjunction with a detailed energy management strategy, effectively optimizes the voltage distribution and minimizes energy waste. Furthermore, a dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) strategy was employed, which adjusts voltage and frequency in response to workload variations. This approach enhances system efficiency by aligning energy use with operational demand, effectively minimizing unnecessary power usage. Additionally, a sleep strategy was implemented to enhance the efficiency of frequency adjustment and reduce the time overhead. Conclusively, simulations and sea trials confirm a substantial 30.75% reduction in energy use by the control system of the underwater glider, boosting its range and endurance by 12.18% and 48.3%, respectively.

articleTitle: A Dyson Brownian Motion Model for Scintillation in Waveguides
abstract: A wave propagating through a random medium develops amplitude fluctuations due to scattering. The scintillation index is much used in the wave propagation literature to describe the variance of the intensity fluctuations across range. At asymp-totically long ranges, the wave intensity is Rayleigh distributed to have a scintillation index of unity. These ranges are called the fully-saturated regime. There are no wave theoretic models that relate the strength of the fluctuations to the ranges for full-saturation. This paper focuses on the scintillation indices of the modes propagating in the waveguide. The scattering in the modes is described using a product of unitary random matrices across range. This paper then describes the product of the matrices as Dyson Brownian Motion (DBM), a well studied topic in random matrix theory. For an infinite number of matrices included in the product, the Brownian motion model predicts that the result would be matrices that fit the Circular Unitary Ensemble (CUE) description. The paper then uses the CUE statistics to predict the intensity and scintillation index of the modes at full saturation. From the DBM model, this paper also relates the ranges for full-saturation to the strength of the fluctuations, and the number of modes propagating in the waveguide.

articleTitle: Synchronization Signal Identification and Parameter Estimation Based on Delay Autocorrelation Method
abstract: The study of non-cooperative underwater acoustic communication (UAC) has attracted more attention from the perspective of information security. Nevertheless, the presence of non-cooperative UAC has faced a significant obstacle mostly due to the uncertainty of non-cooperative subjects engaged in the communication process. This challenge is further intertwined with other adverse variables, such as substantial multipath and Doppler effects in the underwater acoustic channel. To tackle this problem, the task of accurately identifying modulation types and effectively estimating the parameters of UAC synchronization signals is a crucial step. The synchronization signal marks the beginning of a frame of data, and in non-cooperative UAC, it enables the identification of data signals that follow it. In this paper, we propose a method based on delay autocorrelation to identify synchronization signals, specifically linear frequency modulation (LFM) signals and hyperbolic frequency modulation (HFM) signals, as well as to estimate their parameters. LFM and HFM signals are often used in UAC for time synchronization because of their favourable anti-Doppler and autocorrelation characteristics. In this method, first, the algorithm of delay autocorrelation is used to identify LFM and HFM by utilizing their different bandwidths within the spectrum. Subsequently, the maximum energy frequency algorithm based on delay au-tocorrelation spectrum is presented for parameter estimation after identification. Furthermore, we analyze the feasibility of the algorithms under multipath channels. The performance of the proposed method has been validated through the simulation and the experiments carried out in an anechoic tank and the sea trial.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of the Capture Chamber Model in Mutriku MOWC Wave Power Plant
abstract: Ocean wave energy has de potential to satisfy 15% of EU energy demand, cutting 136 MT/MWh off the CO2 emissions by 2050, as stated by the EU Energy Road Map. Analogously, the Spanish Renewable Energies Plan specifically highlighted the Spanish marine energy potential with special emphasis in wave energy. In this context, Oscillating Water Column (OWC) converters are maybe nowadays the most promising wave energy converters, with the potential capability of sea energy harnessing from diverse on-shore and floating structures. This paper presents an analytic modeling of the wave capture chamber for a fixed on-shore OWC wave power plant. The model is particularized and parameterized for the case of the Mutriku MOWC wave power plant, located in the Spanish Basque Country coast, and then validated using both measured real wave entry data and experimental generated output power from the plant

articleTitle: A DVL Measurement Correction Method in High Dynamic Environment and its Application for SINS/DVL Integrated Navigation
abstract: Aiming at the degradation of strapdown inertial navigation system (SINS)/ Doppler velocity log (DVL) integrated navigation accuracy under high maneuvering conditions, a new SINS/DVL tightly integrated navigation algorithm for high dynamic environment is proposed. Firstly, based on the DVL measurement principle, the relationship between DVL frequency shift and AUV instantaneous velocity is constructed. The SINS high precision measurement information in short time are utilized to compensate for the motion changes. And a new DVL measurement error correct method is obtained. Then, the SINS/DVL tightly integrated navigation framework is redesigned based on the proposed error compensation method under high dynamic environment. The simulation and sea trial are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Enhanced LoRaWan Adaptive Data Rate for Mobile Devices in Harsh Marine Environment
abstract: LoRaWAN uses adaptive data rate (ADR) algorithm to allocate appropriate transmission rate and transmission power for static terminal equipment, which increases the overall capac-ity of the network and reduces power consumption. However, the standard ADR algorithm is only applicable under the condition of stable channel quality, and lacks consideration of external environment changes. Especially in the marine environment, due to the influence of end-devices movement and wave fluctuation, the channel transmission loss is usually in a state of rapid change. This leads to the problems that the transmission rate and transmission power allocated to end-device by ADR algorithm do not match the new environment, resulting in packet loss and energy efficiency decline. Therefore, this paper proposes a new ADR algorithm called dynamic-Kalman ADR (DK-ADR). The algorithm uses Kalman filter to solve the problem that the signal-to-noise ratio of network server received packets changes rapidly, thus solving the problems of high packet loss rate and low energy efficiency of standard ADR algorithm in harsh environment. We conducted simulation modeling to evaluate the performance of DK-ADR, and compared our results with three alternative solutions ADR, ADR+ and G-ADR. The simulation results show that compared with standard ADR, the Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) of our scheme is increased by 477%, and compared with the best competitor (G-ADR), the PDR is increased by 21 %, even for mobile end-devices in harsh marine environment. In addition, compared with standard ADR, the Energy Consumption per Packet Delivered (ECPD) decreased by 80%, slightly better than G-ADR.

articleTitle: Unmanned Boat Motion Prediction Based on GRU-SVR Model
abstract: External environmental factors such as sea wind and waves can affect the motion of unmanned boats. In order to ensure the safe navigation of unmanned boats, it is significant to predict the motion of unmanned boats in advance to take control measures. A combination model of GRU-SVR is proposed for predicting the motion of unmanned boats and conducts single-step prediction. Firstly, the real ship data is preprocessed and used as inputs to the combination model. Secondly, Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) and Support Vector Regression (SVR) are used for single-step prediction, and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is used to optimize the groups of weights on the training data. Finally, when testing, the k-nearest neighbor (KNN) algorithm is used to combine the predicted values of the single models to obtain the final prediction. Experimental results show that, compared to single GRU and SVR models, the GRU-SVR combination model has higher prediction accuracy. Obtaining the motion attitude of unmanned boats in advance is of great significance for the motion control and safe navigation of unmanned boats.

articleTitle: Experimental Approach on Structural Stability and Turbidity Propagation around Landing Units in Deep-Sea Mining
abstract: Mankind's increasing demand for rare earths and metals is surpassing the capacity of mainland resources, prompting exploration into deep-sea deposits as a potential solution. However, these opportunities come with unique challenges in terms of environmental protecting. Sediment plumes, generated by mining machinery, have been identified as one of the major problems for the surrounding ecosystem. To address this issue, a vertical and minimally invasive approach is to be developed for the degradation of seafloor massive sulfides. To prove the functionality of the selected measures, a smart monitoring system is developed. In this paper the applicability of the developed measurement system for the detection of sediment plumes is investigated. Additionally, experiments on the structural integrity of a 1:20 trench cutter model during the landing and loading process are conducted.

articleTitle: REX 18 – Robotic Exercises 2018 Multi-robot field trials
abstract: This paper describes the tests performed with three different systems during the annual REX exercise, organized by the Portuguese Navy to provide a testing ground for tests, data gathering, and demonstration of systems developed by universities, research centers, and small enterprises. During REX18, the tests performed concerned a USV/UAV team used for search and rescue, an autonomous sailing boat used for surveillance, and a system of passive hydrophones for monitoring motorboats.

articleTitle: Study on Hydrodynamics and Wake Structures of a Fast and Big Thunniform Fish Robot
abstract: This paper analyzes undulating and oscillating motion of fish through numerical simulations, exploring correlations between fin thrust and swimming speed. Employing kinematic equations for motion control in computational fluid dynamics, the study highlights a reduction in power demand with oscillation, making it effective for achieving desired speeds despite energy loss. The dynamics of undulating fins in aquatic and aerial locomotion remain insufficiently understood. The study explores the trade-off between energy-consuming, highly propulsive movements, and simpler, faster movements, requiring sophisticated design techniques to reduce volume. The geometry, developed with Rhino 6 software, incorporates fluid resistance calculations using Ansys Fluent 19. Emphasizing flow velocities from 1 to $4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, with a focus on the critical velocity of $3.6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$-an essential parameter for shaping the future design of underwater robotic fish. Critical factors such as flexibility, viscosity, and shape change were examined for their effect on efficiency enhancement.

articleTitle: Bridging the Sim-to-Real GAP for Underwater Image Segmentation
abstract: Labeling images for every new task or data pattern a model needs to learn is a significant time bottleneck in real-world applications. Moreover, acquiring the necessary data for training the models can be challenging. Ideally, one would train the models with simulated images and adapt them for the desired real tasks using the least possible amount of data. Active learning can be used to solve this problem with minimal effort. In this work, we train SegFormer for pipeline segmentation with synthetic images from an underwater simulated environment and fine-tune the model with real underwater pipeline images recorded in a marina. The evaluation shows that selecting real data with active learning for fine-tuning the model gives better results than randomly selecting the images. As part of the work, we release the dataset recorded in the marina, MarinaPipe, which will be publicly available.

articleTitle: Media Access Control Protocol for Submarine Static Target Detection with a Multi-AUV Cluster
abstract: Due to the challenges for the underwater acoustic channel, designing an efficient media access control (MAC) protocol to enhance the underwater transmission efficiency is very important. In this paper, we design a task-oriented MAC protocol, called as underwater ALOHA protocol adapted for submarine static target detection (UW-ALOHA-USTD) protocol, for submarine static target detection with a multi-AUV cluster. In the proposed MAC protocol, a frame is divided two sub-frames, where sub-frame 1 is used for the underwater localization and cluster state information exchange, sub-frame 2 is responsible for transmitting task data. By introducing a conflict avoidance mechanism and improving the UW-ALOHA protocol, the proposed protocol effectively reduces data transmission conflict and delay, as well as enhancing the data transmission success rate. Simulation result shows that the proposed UW-ALOHA-USTD protocol performs well, and provides an efficient and reliable data transmission solution for submarine static target detection with a multi-AUV cluster.

articleTitle: On the Observation of Water Bodies by Means of Compact Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar Imagery
abstract: Water bodies, including lakes and rivers, represent extraor-dinary sources for ecology, biodiversity, irrigation and water supply. As a matter of fact, they impact on several aspects of human, animal and vegetation living. Hence, continuous and reliable monitoring of the water bodies extent is of paramount importance and must be performed by high-quality techno-logical tools. Spaceborne detection of changes associated to natural and human-induced water dynamics is of great im-portance for ecosystem preservation, disaster warnings and water conservation projects. For this purpose, it is well estab-lished that satellite remote sensing tools represent an invalu-able source of information. Under this framework, this study focuses on the analysis of compact-polarimetric (CP) C-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging modes to extract lake shoreline and, therefore, monitor the water-covered area. A reference shoreline extraction scheme is adopted for this purpose, which is feed by po-larimetric features associated to the correlation of backseat-tering channels, namely δ. The lake Athabasca in Alberta, Canada, is selected as a meaningful test site. The experimen-tal results show that the CP C-band SAR measurements can be effectively used to get lake extent information.

articleTitle: A Multi-Stage Visual Positioning Method for Autonomous Underwater Docking
abstract: Due to limited battery and storage space, the Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) need to complete docking with the subsea docking station (SDS) for charging and data transmission. To ensure successful docking, accurate terminal positioning is crucial. We propose a novel multi-stage visual positioning method that segments terminal navigation into two distinct stages, focusing on different targets: active lights and passive markers. Additionally, we incorporate a neural network to augment the algorithm's robustness, thereby enabling AUVs to achieve whole-process high-precision positioning. The efficacy of our positioning approach has been substantiated through in-air testing, and the viability of our medium-range positioning algorithm has been demonstrated through underwater trials. The forthcoming phase involves integrating this algorithm into the AUV's system to execute actual docking task.

articleTitle: A Distributed “Any-Communication” Task Allocation Approach to Information-Based Planning Underwater
abstract: Autonomous ocean monitoring poses a unique challenge due to the dynamic and restrictive underwater environment. Distributed adaptive sampling can address many of the challenges of a large and evolving system; however, it typically requires strong assumptions on the communicability of the agents. This paper's goal is to propose a novel “Any-Communication” approach to performing distributed adaptive sampling under limiting communication conditions, including the underwater space, through using a task allocation approach to information-based planning and a communication-robust distributed solver. The approach is verified against multiple randomized simulated trials, and the resultant improvement in optimality is compared against a naive distributed approach. The trials indicate that when under a simple linear cost agent model, the approach can provide up to 30% reduction in agent operational cost. More importantly, the improvement is proportional to the availability of communication. This works indicates the potential of the “Any-Communication” approach to distributed information-based planning under limited communication.

articleTitle: Designing of Preamble Signal for the Integrated Underwater Communication and Positioning
abstract: Traditionally, two sets of independent communication and positioning systems are equipped on the underwater vehicle. However, it is unfavorable for the miniaturization and lightweight requirements of the underwater vehicle. Therefore, the integrated underwater communication and positioning has been becoming a hot research topic in recent years. In this paper, a preamble signal composed of two superimposed Hyperbolic frequency modulation signals is designed for the integrated underwater communication and positioning system. Moreover, the multiuser identification is also considered in the preamble design. A joint Doppler factor and signal arrival time estimation method is developed with the designed preamble signal. Simulation results show that the joint estimation method using the designed preamble signal performs well.

articleTitle: Event-Based Distributed Control for Multiple Fully-Actuated MSVs Under Prescribed Performance Constraints
abstract: This study addresses a complex challenge concerning event-based leader-follower distributed control for multiple fully-actuated MSVs in the presence of uncertain dynamics, time-varying environmental disturbances, and prescribed performance constraints. Initially, a performance constraint is imposed on the neighborhood errors, and the utilization of radial basis function neural networks (RBF NNs) is proposed to handle overall modeling uncertainties. Time-varying environmental disturbances are mitigated through the application of a nonlinear disturbance observer. Additionally, an event-based distributed control strategy is presented, and a trigger threshold condition was designed to facilitate discrete information transfer among MSVs system. The comprehensive analysis of Lyapunov theory demonstrates the boundedness of all signals within the closed-loop system. Finally, the effectiveness of the designed control strategy is verified through numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Azimuth Direction of Arrival Estimation Using Near-Surface Tilted Arrays in Deep-Sea Bottom-Bounce Area
abstract: The bottom bounce mode plays a crucial role in underwater acoustic detection in the shadow zone of deep water. When both the source and hydrophone are situated at depths of 300 meters or shallower, the main contributions to the sound field come from four multipath rays that reflected by the bottom only once. The sound field in the shadow zone mostly consists of larger- angle rays. Under such conditions, when the bottom bounce sound is received by a vertical line array, the lack of azimuthal resolution prevents obtaining source azimuth information. When the bottom bounce sound is received by a horizontal line array, an azimuth deviation appears because of the coupling effect between elevation angle and azimuth angle. This paper explains the reasons for the deviation. Then based on the trigonometric relation between the elevation angle and the azimuth angle, the deviation could be modified by the tilted array. The method is demonstrated with the simulated result.

articleTitle: Optimal Dam Release Requirements for Tenualosa Ilisha Fish Migration in the Narmada Estuary: A Numerical Modeling Approach
abstract: Estuaries, acting as vital transition zones between freshwater and marine environments, play a crucial role as productive ecosystems and nurseries for various species. Governed by river discharge and tidal variations, estuarine dynamics are significantly impacted by human interventions, such as dam construction. Dams, while essential for water management, alter river flow patterns and negatively affect downstream estuarine ecosystems. This study focuses on the Narmada estuary, where the construction of the Sardar Sarovar Dam has disrupted estuarine dynamics, particularly affecting the anadromous migration of Hilsa fish. Hilsa, contributing significantly to local fishermen's income, relies on the estuary for breeding. The research employs the TELEMAC2D model to assess the impact of controlled discharge from the dam on tidal dynamics and identifies optimal flow conditions for effective fish migration. Results indicate that discharge rates between 1500 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/s and 2250 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/s promote favorable conditions for fish migration, while a minimum flow of 500 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/s is required to prevent tidal dominance. The study also found that allowing Hilsa fishing beyond 70 kilometers from the river mouth is harmful to juveniles and livebearers due to limited tidal flushing and their freshwater dependent stage of life. Additionally, figured out that maintaining the optimal discharge rate during the migration period can enhance fish production in the subsequent year. This conference paper extends the findings presented in our prior publication in Ecological Indicators (Vengadesan et al., 2023).

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Potential Environmental Impacts from an Offshore Wind Energy Farm in the Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Following the desire to reduce the energy dependence from fossil fuels, plants supplied by renewable energy sources are spreading worldwide. Among the current technologies, a new frontier is represented by offshore wind energy, thanks to the possibility to increase the capacity factor, and consequently the income from the investment, and at the same time overcome the problem of finding places without environmental constrictions. In this context, some new projects are currently under investigation in Italy, proposing the installation of floating wind farms, due to the deep seabed. For this reason, this manuscript evaluates the potential impacts related to the construction of a new big offshore wind farm, located in the Mediterranean Sea. The LCA methodology is applied to the case study.

articleTitle: An Array Calibration Method based on Beam Pattern and Neural Network in Underwater USBL System
abstract: In underwater localization scenarios, especially for the ultra short baseline (USBL) system, array calibration is essential. The localization performance may decrease rapidly when the array coordinate deviation exists. The main drawbacks of conventional calibration methods are the fact that they usually require a large amount of measurements, so the time-saving calibration methods are demanded in practical application scenarios. Motivated by the fact that neural networks' efficiency in learning nonlinear relationship, we propose the calibration method based on beam pattern and neural network, which can achieve one measurement in calibration procedure. Differential beam pattern model is used to generate the training data. Simultaneously, the array errors are modeled in polar coordinates form, corresponding radius and angle deviations for each array element. The performance of calibration is evaluated based on the estimated accuracy of sound source's direction of arrival (DoA) after calibration. Both the simulation and experiment results have verified our proposed method, ledding to an average 46.5% error reduction in the DoA estimation during the experiments when compared with traditional method.

articleTitle: Research on Unbalance Force and Stability of Rotary Energy Recovery Device in Seawater Reverse Osmosis System
abstract: Rotary energy recovery device (RERD) that reduces energy consumption from the pressurizing seawater plays an important role in the seawater reverse osmosis desalination system. The rotating progress of the rotor, which is the key part of the RERD, is affected by the lateral unbalance force generated by the non-uniform flow state of the liquid in the circular clearance. In this paper, the flowing characteristics and the cause of lateral force in the clearance were analyzed by CFD. Thus, the pressure distribution curve around the outer wall of the rotor and the character of pressure fluctuation was obtained. Moreover, the influence of the operating pressure was calculated and analyzed. The results showed that the pressure distribution around the outer wall of the rotor presents sinusoidal distribution and it is related to the unbalanced force. Meanwhile, the uniformity and stability of the pressure distribution change with the operating pressure. This research provides a method to predict the stability of the RERD, which will be of great significance for improving the unstable problem of the device in the design stage.

articleTitle: Slender Light Array Guidance for UUV Formation Keeping and Communication
abstract: Unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) plays an increasingly important role in marine scientific research, ocean engineering operations, and military fields due to its autonomy, flexibility, and versatility. Autonomous intelligent formation is an important development direction for the future new concept UUV, which puts forward higher requirements for the comprehensive perception ability of UUV in underwater scenes. UUV formation can achieve rapid transmission of large-capacity information and task collaboration over short distances, which is of great strategic significance. The traditional formation keeping method based on acoustic communication has poor stability, high delay, and low security, and is difficult to adapt to the complex underwater environment with weak communication. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an optical tracking and formation keeping method based on slender light array, and verifies the effectiveness of the method through pool simulation tests. However, UUV formation is different from aerial drone formation, as it has higher challenges and environmental complexity. Due to the rapid attenuation of radio signals underwater, most airborne sensors, such as GPS and WIFI, are not available underwater. The commonly used underwater acoustic communication positioning equipment, such as ultra-short baseline positioning system (USBL), has high time delay and non-Gaussian error, which brings great difficulties to UUV formation [4]. It is difficult to achieve precise navigation of UUV in formations solely relying on the inertial navigation system (SINS). So for the UUV formation, there are generally three stages, as shown in Fig. 1. S1 is the approach navigation stage that only relies on inertial navigation system (INS), S2 is the ultra-short baseline (USBL) acoustic guidance [5]–[6] and position correction stage, and S3 is the optical guidance [7]–[9] and formation keeping stage (it is the main research stage of this paper). The red line represents the INS working timeline, the blue line represents the acoustic guidance working timeline, and the green line represents the optical guidance timeline. After entering the S3 stage, the leader follower strategy [10] can be used to maintain the formation. In addition, it can be seen from the Fig. 1 that these three stages have overlapping areas on the timeline, and acoustic, optical, and INS information can also be fused to improve the formation performance [11]–[12]. In response to the problem of limited underwater acoustic communication and the inability to complete formation, this paper adds a UUV broadside slender light array in the S3 stage to provide optical guidance for formation construction and keeping, as shown in Fig. 2. As is well known, positioning is crucial for achieving a high-precision formation. However, due to the complex underwater environment, radio signals are extremely fast underwater, making it difficult for UUV to achieve fast and accurate collaborative operations like USV and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). The relatively mature UUV formation scheme now is to use underwater acoustic communication for positioning, and the communication delay is interpolated or compensated by inertial navigation. This method is beneficial for the constitution of UUV formation during long-distance stages (S1 and S2 as shown in Fig. 2), but not conducive to maintaining formations at close range and for a long time. This is mainly due to the fact that UUV swarms are prone to entering acoustic communication blind spots at close range, leading to an increase in positioning errors, and the inertial navigation errors of individual UUV are also accumulating. However, underwater optical communication positioning does not have these drawbacks at close range, and it has become a hot research technology in the field of UUV both domestically and internationally. The remaining sections of the paper are organized as follows: details about proposed method in Section II, experimental results will be discussed in Section III, and of which conclusions are summarized in Section IV.

articleTitle: Selection of a Renewable Energy Mix by using Economic and Environmental Criteria. A Case Study in the Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Despite technological progress and the ever more stringent laws on polluting emissions, in several remote areas and small islands the energy production is still dominated by the utilization of fossil fuels. This article discusses the feasibility of a mixed system of renewable sources (wind, photovoltaic and wave energy) to be implemented in Favignana, considering alternatively the minimization of the energy costs and estimation of the CO2 emission of the proposed energy mix. The study was carried out by estimating the energy production on a monthly and annual basis considering a mix of three renewable sources. This method can be easily applied for several small islands, estimating the ability to reduce the energy production from fossil fuels.

articleTitle: COLREG Compliant Collision Avoidance System for an Unmanned Surface Vehicle
abstract: The increasing development of Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) for various applications in open and shallow waters has increased demand for more advanced USVs with improved safety and navigation systems. This article introduces a collision avoidance system for USVs that complies with the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREG) rules, particularly rules 13 to 18 from Part B - Steering and Sailing. The system utilizes a three-block architecture for risk assessment, situation identification, and path replanning. Practical testing and validation were conducted using the Stonefish simulator, demonstrating the system's effectiveness in ensuring compliance with COLREG rules and facilitating safe navigation of USVs.

articleTitle: Human-Like Automatic Berthing System Based on Imitative Trajectory Plan and Tracking Control
abstract: Automatic berthing is a key technology to reduce the burden on navigation officers and resolve labor shortage. Since berthing involves collision risks against quays and other ships, it requires reliable maneuver like skilled captains do. In recent years, various approaches using optimal control [1]–[3], neural networks (NNs) [4]–[6], or other methods [7]–[8], have been presented to achieve automatic berthing. Despite such great efforts, it is still difficult to demonstrate that berthing by a machine is as safe and reliable as that by human captains.

articleTitle: Improving SONAR Image Classification Performance Via Denoising
abstract: Acoustic imaging SONAR systems have diverse applications in marine technology, encompassing mapping the seabed, locating shipwrecks, identifying potential areas for resource extraction, monitoring the marine environment, facilitating underwater navigation, and aiding in obstacle avoidance. The technology has witnessed significant advancements with deep neural networks in recent years. However, numerous challenges arise in the automatic, deep learning-based underwater SONAR image classification due to poor resolution, low contrast, sub-stantial interference, serious speckle noise, and insufficient data availability. Integrating deep neural networks into underwater SONAR image classification can enable real-time decision-making, crucial in marine resource exploration, environmental protection, and navigation. SONAR image classification is a vital tool for navigation, detection, and scientific research in aquatic environments. Classifying SONAR images is a challenging task compared to other image classification tasks. In this work, our focus is on reducing the noise in SONAR images that seriously limits the classifier's performance. The noise in SONAR images arises from various factors, such as marine life, water turbulence, and sensor limitations, leading to ambiguous and unclear images. This complexity makes it difficult to distinguish among different features and objects. Leveraging the denoised SONAR images during the training of the classifier improves classification accuracy. Extensive simulations using different classifiers validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Development of Desktop-Size Marine Swarm Research Platform
abstract: Research in aquatic environments often demands extensive facilities, specialized knowledge, and dedicated support staff, which are expensive and usually out of reach for smaller research teams. Establishing accessible research infrastructure, especially with testbeds and freely available software, can reduce entry barriers, shorten the time to implementation, and lessen the likelihood of failure in challenging underwater settings. To address these limitations in aquatic research, we have developed the Marine Automatic Swarm Experiment Platform (MASEP). MASEP is a tabletop-sized, marine swarm robotics testbed for evaluating underwater robotic swarm controllers, novel communication strategies, and more in a simulated aquatic environment. Through MASEP, we have successfully demonstrated the tracking and control of multiple robots, as well validated the robustness and reliability of an external visual localization system when fused with onboard sensor data. By enabling multi-robot tracking in a miniature, low-cost platform, MASEP opens up new possibilities for the advancement of underwater robot swarm testing and the development of effective control algorithms.

articleTitle: A CNN-based Hybrid Dehazing and Regression Model for Sea Surface Wind Speed Retrieval from Rain-contaminated Marine Radar Data
abstract: In recent years, the widespread application of X-band radar for measuring ocean surface parameters has become common, yet the presence of rain significantly hinders the marine radar system. As a result, this paper introduces a model that combines the dehazing technique with the convolutional neural network (CNN) regression network to estimate sea surface wind speed from X-band radar images collected under rainy conditions. Specifically, the CNN-based end-to-end dehazing system is first applied to the rain-contaminated radar images to mitigate the blurred areas caused by rain. Then, a deep CNN regression network is utilized to estimate the wind speed. The radar data were collected from a shipborne Decca radar in a sea area 300 km from Halifax, Canada, in 2008. In contrast to the wind speed estimation method based on support vector regression (SVR), the utilization of the CNN network demonstrates superior accuracy in wind speed measurement, yielding more precise results. The root-mean-square error (RMSE) of the estimated result from the Decca radar data is decreased to 1.02 m/s from 1.24 m/s, and the correlation coefficient (CC) is increased to 0.95 from 0.91.

articleTitle: A Phase Unwrapping Algorithm based on Periodicity Extension
abstract: Phase estimation is of great significance for the azimuth estimation using hydrophone arrays. For high-frequency signal sources, it is often challenging to estimate the phase differences between the received signals of the array elements when the element spacing is much larger than the signal wavelength. A phase unwrapping algorithm based on periodicity extension is proposed here, which leverages the periodic nature of the wrapped phase to obtain accurate phase information while avoiding error accumulation. By directly retrieving the phase matrix and applying quality judgment and predictive correction, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated via restoring ambiguity integers. Experimental results validate the performance of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Development of a Low-Cost Coastal Cabled Underwater Camera Observatory as Part of ANERIS Project: Preliminary Design and Results
abstract: This paper presents the process of building a low-cost, cabled underwater camera observatory with applications in coastal areas. This includes an underwater camera, and external sensor interface, external LED light controller, and an anti-biofouling wiper mechanism connected by a cable to a central hub stationed on land which makes all relevant data openly accessible via internet. The proposed setup allows for seamless integration of additional external sensors, thanks to its open-source nature. The low-cost underwater observatory is intended to be a proof-of-concept of an affordable, open-source, and easily reproducible system that has as few tool requirements as possible, and is part of a larger ANERIS research project which aims at developing innovative technologies towards operational marine biology. This hopes to ensure that the majority of interested parties are capable of building a similar system without needing to invest sizable capital in custom part orders and/or tools. The design includes mostly commercial off the shelf components and an anti-biofouling mechanism based on a magnetically coupled wiper. Experimental results from a one week deployment in Oslofjord are presented.

articleTitle: Distributed Trajectory Estimation for Multi-Autonomous Underwater Vehicle
abstract: Multi-AUV collaboration is significant in marine resource exploration, submarine scientific observation and underwater rescue. However, limited communication bandwidth and acoustic range challenge trajectory estimation of A UVs. In this paper, we design a distributed multi-AUV system and implement an optimizer based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). In our system, each AUV is required to meet and exchange information with others locally. This optimizer treats measurements between AUVs as constraints and transforms the global optimization problem into multiple sub-problems, which allows each AUV to optimize its trajectory independently. Compared with a representative algorithm on the same dataset, this approach effectively reduces the optimization time and improves the convergence efficiency while ensuring convergence accuracy.

articleTitle: Instance Segmentation for Active Sonar Image Based on Image Segmentation Foundation Model
abstract: Through instance segmentation techniques, fore-ground objects in active sonar images are segmented based on their categories, aiding in the recognition and understanding of the seafloor conditions. However, due to the scarcity of datasets for active sonar image segmentation, the results of sonar image instance segmentation are not satisfactory. Recently, Segment Anything Model (SAM) by Meta demonstrated remarkable segmentation capabilities leveraging its vast training dataset, Segment Anything 1-Billion mask dataset (SA-1B). Yet, SAM struggles to achieve complete segmentation of sonar image targets, lacks classification capabilities, and its results heavily depend on the type, position, and number of prompts. This paper integrates SAM with traditional instance segmentation models, using the SAM model to enhance the performance of active sonar image object detection and instance segmentation, achieving notable results.

articleTitle: Soundscaping Using a Smart Cable Prototype Off the Coast of Portugal
abstract: Ocean soundscaping is an important tool to monitor ocean noise and to understand how it may impact marine life. A promising approach is the exploration of the SMART cable concept that relies on the use of a telecommunication cable equipped with environmental sensors, allowing for ocean real-time monitoring. The K2D project<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> Knowledge and Data from the Deep Space, FCT-MIT Portugal, contract no. 045941. developed a set of cable nodes with extended SMART capabilities. These nodes were tested on a short telecommunication cable deployed off the coast of Sesimbra, Portugal. In this sea trial, several ocean variables were gathered, including underwater sound that was used to characterize the region's soundscape. Three types of analysis were conducted: a) the evaluation of the usual noise level baseline for all nodes, b) an attempt of sound source identification through frequency band analysis, and c) the evaluation of the noise level in different periods of the day. The results show that node 1 (the closest to shore) has higher noise levels and no significant difference between day and night periods in the frequency bands between 100 Hz and 1 kHz. No biological signatures were identified in the recorded data. Comparing the three nodes' locations, the results suggest that the area where node 1 was deployed is the most affected by (coastal) ship traffic.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Newly Developed Twin-Hybrid Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (THAUV) using Integrated Airfoil and Elevator
abstract: In this paper, a new type of multi-body type twin hybrid autonomous underwater vehicle(THAUV) was introduced. THAUV includes pair of buoyancy engines, thrusters, and elevators for movement. Buoyancy engine was designed Elevators were included to control the attitude of the THAUV and increase the maneuverability. Mechanical and electronical hardware was designed and manufactured. The experiment was conducted, and the result was compared to the simulation result to confirm the affect of elevators.

articleTitle: Cross-Layer-based Opportunistic Routing for Underwater Acoustic-Optical Hybrid Networks
abstract: In the past few decades, underwater acoustic networks have been widely studied and applied due to the advantages of long transmission distance of acoustic links. However their development has been limited by high delay and low data rates. Underwater wireless optical communication provides a potential alternative transmission link with a high data rate. However, it has the disadvantage of short transmission distance. In this paper, we proposed a cross-layer-based opportunistic routing for underwater hybrid acoustic-optical networks (AOCLOR). The sending node selects the sector candidate area based on the position and number of neighbor nodes and quickly sends packets over the optical link. The forwarding nodes are determined by the opportunistic routing, where the acoustic links are responsible for sending notification packets and node position information. Simulation results have shown that the proposed AO-CLOR protocol can not only improve the data rate, but also ensure the packet delivery ratio in underwater acoustic-optical hybrid networks.

articleTitle: Dictionary-based Spread-Spectrum Modulation for Covert Underwater Acoustic Communications
abstract: A covert underwater acoustic waveform is presented. The modulation scheme is based on a pseudo-random selection of spread-spectrum sequences from a dictionary. A specific aspect of this scheme is that each sequence has a distinct chip rate. The use of spreading sequences is a means of operating at low SNR, while the use of different chip rates strongly attenuates the cyclostationary signature, the objective being to maximize the robustness against eavesdropping attacks. Simulation results and sea trials show that communication can be successful at negative SNRs while being robust to cyclostationary analysis.

articleTitle: Path Planning and Control for Remotely Operated Vehicles Focused on Autonomous Visual Inspection of Floating Offshore Wind Structure
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to address the challenges of inspecting offshore wind turbines by presenting a real-time dynamic path-planning system for remotely operated vehicles (ROVs). Focused on floating wind turbine structures, the proposed methodology integrates an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) into the structure, allowing dynamic adjustment of the inspection path based on real-time pose data. Utilizing a fault-tolerant control solution, the system enables autonomous flight control of ROVs, maintaining consistent orientation towards the structure and desired inspection distance. The applicability of the approach is validated through simulations in the OceanRINGS+ control suite, emphasizing the importance of dynamic path planning in enhancing efficiency, safety, and cost-effectiveness in offshore wind turbine inspections.

articleTitle: A Novel Reactive Control Using Maximum Power Tracking for Wave Energy Converter
abstract: Ocean energy heavily depends on environmental conditions, making extracting maximum power more complex and challenging. A novel adaptable reactive control is proposed for a linear wave generator. Based on the theory, the maximum output power is extracted when the excitation force and wave speed are in resonance. However, the phase between excitation force and velocity depends on the wave period, where it keeps changing. In this paper, the intrinsic impedance of the linear machine is analyzed at every wave period. Since the maximum power can be regulated at the electrical terminal using power electronic devices, the electrical impedance can counteract the phase difference between the excitation force and the velocity. The novel maximum power tracking algorithm is proposed based on the estimated phase difference between voltage and current. The benefit of the proposed method is that the additional configuration is not required, and more power can be extracted.

articleTitle: International Management of Underwater Noise Pollution in the Northeast Atlantic
abstract: Underwater noise pollution is increasingly recognised by marine regulators and policymakers as a significant threat to marine ecosystems. Noise pollution can travel tens or even thousands of kilometres, traversing international boundaries and affecting animals which may themselves range across multiple jurisdictions. For these reasons, international cooperation is considered necessary to manage this pollution effectively. However, measures to monitor, assess and reduce noise pollution at these large scales are still in their infancy. In the Northeast Atlantic, substantive monitoring of underwater noise pollution began in 2015 through the OSPAR Convention, an intergovernmental organisation through which states in this region coordinate marine environmental policy. This paper reviews the progress made since then, highlighting lessons learned and setting out the remaining challenges for effective international noise management in this region. It is hoped that these experiences may prove useful for colleagues in other jurisdictions.

articleTitle: Design and Experiments of a low-cost Small Remotely Operated Vehicle System Prototype
abstract: With the development of remotely operated vehicle (ROV) technology, the tasks conducted by ROV are increasingly complex, which imposes heightened demands on the quality of the ROV human-computer interaction mechanism (HCI). Therefore, considering the aforementioned and the research objectives of our team, we have designed and developed a low-cost small ROV system prototype. The novel ROV system architecture(SA) is introduced herein. A series of field experiments are conducted, and the results demonstrate that the ROV can successfully perform its fundamental functions (general maneuvering, camera imaging, data collection/recording and ROV parameter configuration) and additional task functions (automatic control and image recognition). It can be concluded that the proposed SA enables the ROV to exhibit exceptional functionality and user-friendliness at a low cost.

articleTitle: Concepts of Resilience Design for Unmanned Marine Systems and Applications on Underwater Glider
abstract: With the continuous advancement of high-performance battery technology and advanced power systems, the performance of unmanned marine systems (UMSs), particularly their endurance, has witnessed a remarkable improvement. However, in complex and extreme marine environments, the influence of uncertainties from multiple sources on long-endurance UMSs is becoming increasingly significant. This can result in performance degradation or even system loss. Therefore, it is crucial to address how these uncertainties can be incorporated into system design and utilized to enhance overall life cycle performance. To tackle this issue, we propose a novel full life cycle design paradigm known as resilience design. Firstly, the concepts, framework, and evaluation index are introduced. Secondly, a case study is presented to demonstrate the application of resilience design on a specific type of underwater glider. Subsequently, a rigorous sea trial is conducted to empirically validate the effectiveness of the proposed resilience design approach. Lastly, future directions for research are summarized.

articleTitle: Extracting Coherent Wavefronts from Ocean Ambient Noise via Beamforming: Experimental Data Analysis
abstract: The time derivative of the noise correlation function between two separated receivers has been used to derive the corresponding time domain Green's functions. This paper mainly analyzes the effectiveness of array beamforming in endfire direction for extracting coherent wavefronts from ocean ambient noise in a complex underwater environement, using the SWellEx-96 experimental data. The use of endfire direction beamforming not only allows for accurate coherent wavefronts extraction but also reduces the accumulation time. Given that different frequency bands correspond to different types of sources, this paper also analyzes the impact of source frequency bands and directions on extracting coherent wavefronts. With coherent wavefronts extracted, a dictionary learning-based method can be applied for sound speed profile inversion.

articleTitle: Novel Reference Trajectories for Improved Marine Surface Vehicle Path Following
abstract: Model Predictive Planner (MPPlan) is a model-based motion planning system developed at the University of New Hampshire to provide autonomous vehicles with real-time path updates. MPPlan provides appropriate waypoints to define the planned surface trajectories similar to that of other conventional path planners and, furthermore, provides additional reference trajectories for a wide range of kinematic states and planned control actuations. This study investigates utilizing this additional a priori knowledge to improve path following controller performance. Here, a path following system that combines proportional line-of-sight guidance with a heading and speed controller is implemented on a micro-ASV using three different levels of kinematic and kinetic input. The system performance is studied across a range of vehicle speeds and environmental forcing conditions, thereby inducing variations in the ASV crab angle in order to study its impact on path-following performance. It is found that the proposed path following system using reference trajectories to take into account the expected surge velocity, crab angle, and nominal thrust actuations, reduces maximum cross track error (XTE) by up to 55% compared to that of a baseline path-following scheme. Providing only the surge velocity and crab angle references, the method reduces maximum cross track error by up to 60% versus the baseline scheme. The ability of information uniquely provided by MPPlan to significantly reduce vehicle XTE during unsteady maneuvers, in turn, reduces the need for large safety envelopes and allows for tighter vehicle navigation in the proximity of potential hazards (e.g., obstacles).

articleTitle: Submarine Escape and Rescue Field Trials with Robotic Systems at the REPMUS 2023 Exercise
abstract: This paper underscores the critical role of evolving tools for underwater search and rescue. Successful submarine crew rescue hinges on detecting, locating, and obtaining detailed information about the submerged vessel. Robotic systems, particularly ROVs and AUVs, emerge as invaluable tools, offering swift deployment times compared to manned submersibles. This study presents findings from Submarine Escape and Rescue (SMER) field trials conducted during the REPMUS 2023 naval military exercise off the west coast of Portugal, showcasing the effectiveness of these tools in real-world emergency situations. An initial multibeam sonar search from the surface with the Mar Porfundo ship was performed, followed by a close detailed inspection and visual survey with the EVA AUV of a target military submarine (NRP Arpão) stationed on the sea bottom.

articleTitle: Direction Finding for Shipborne HFSWR based on Integral Reconstruction and Virtual Array Transformation
abstract: Shipborne high-frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) has been widely studied due to its good maneuverability and great advantages in maritime detection and monitoring. However, due to the limitations of the platform space, the placement of radar array is often irregular, which affects the detection performance, especially the direction finding (DF) performance of radar systems. In order to improve the DF performance of the array, this paper proposes a method of combining covariance matrix reconstruction with conjugate virtual array conversion to improve beamforming and expand the array aperture, thereby enhancing the DF performance of the array. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method was verified through simulation experiments and on-site data experiments.

articleTitle: Learning an End-To-End Policy for AUV Control Within Just Forty Minutes Using Parallel Simulation
abstract: Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) has become an essential tool for ocean environmental observation due to their cost-effective integration of various sensors. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) offers a promising solution for complex underwater problems, yet encounters limitations in sample efficiency. This paper presents a distributed parallel framework utilizing multi-threading and parallel simulations within Gazebo to overcome the constraint, leading to a significant acceleration in the training process. The framework can be used as a general training simulation platform for training policy to control underwater vehicle, helping improving autonomous ability of AUV facing complex underwater environment through state-of-the-art DRL algorithm. To verify its capability, a challenging docking control policy for AUV is trained using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. The total time consumption in training process is less than forty minutes, achieving remarkable speed improvements compared to existing methods. This framework holds the potential to expedite the development of AUV control algorithms and enhance the autonomy of AUV in complex environments.

articleTitle: Environment-Based Performance Optimization for Passive Sonar Network
abstract: The ocean environment exhibits temporal and spatial variability. Sonar detection performance is affected by the underwater environment, leading to significant uncertainties. According to the sonar equation, precise predictions of propagation loss will enhance the accuracy of sonar detection performance forecasts, which will help decision making and sonar deployment. However, existing works often simplify propagation loss, either by considering only expansion loss or by treating sensors as a “cookie-cutter” model, introducing inaccuracies. In this paper, we predict the detection performance of passive sonars based on sound speed field forecasts provided by the FVCOM model. We calculated the detection range of a passive sonar at different positions and directions. Multiple passive towed arrays mounted on wave gliders constitute a passive sonar network. By leveraging more reliable sonar performance predictions in the specific region, we optimize the positioning of wave gliders for deployment based on maximum coverage area metrics.

articleTitle: Underwater Noise Reduction by Blade Tip Optimization of a Ship Propeller
abstract: URN induced by ship propeller cavitation is predicted by the permeable FWH acoustic analogy method using near-field hydrodynamic flow as equivalent noise sources. Hydrodynamic flow around a propeller is simulated by CFD with an Eulerian multiphase model and an interphase mass transfer model in the behind-hull condition. URN calculations are validated against cavitation tunnel test results for a 5-bladed propeller on a single-screw work vessel as a test case. The blade tip geometry of the baseline propeller is modified by shape optimization based on steady CFD simulations with simplified hull wake for reducing tip vortex strength without losing propulsive efficiency. The CFD simulations on a large number of design variants show that reducing tip vortex strength more than a certain level leads to an efficiency loss. It implies a trade-off relationship between URN and GHG emission. The numerical predictions of unsteady cavitation and URN are made on the optimized propeller design with the full hull wake model. The comparison shows a noticeable reduction of the cavity volume, which leads to significant decrease of URN at harmonics of BPF compared to the baseline propeller.

articleTitle: Robust Monocular Visual SLAM of Multiple Autonomous Underwater Vehicles against the Keypoint Loss
abstract: This study proposes a robust monocular Visual SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) system against keypoint loss through the cooperation of multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). AUVs do not require human control and can navigate flexibly in underwater environments, but they need to measure their positions based on environmental maps to maintain their autonomy. SLAM is an important element for this. This study adopted ORB-SLAM, a monocular camera-based Visual SLAM that is not expensive, has high processing speed, and is robust against rotation and distortion of the camera image. However, in underwater environments, keypoints are easily lost due to the presence of many dynamic objects such as fish, or lower luminosity than on land. ORB-SLAM has the problem that if keypoints are lost, position estimation becomes impossible and the environmental map is reset. In this study, a small AUV (child AUV) makes maps based on ORB-SLAM. Once it has lost keypoints and is unable to estimate its state, it can receive relative positioning support from an AUV that is capable of accurate state estimation without any external support (parent AUV), thus it can achieve continuous state estimation. The child AUV then generates maps uninterruptedly when it can recognize keypoints again. Simulations using videos of the underwater environment acquired by the AUV were conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Charting the Path to Stronger and More Stable International Environmental Agreements: Insights from Mathematical Modelling and Game Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of citizens' attitudes towards climate change and environmental risk to assess their influence on their governments' willingness to comply with their obligations under the International Environmental Agreements (IEAs). Through mathematical modelling and game theory, the study reveals that citizens' attitudes are not maintained for sufficiently long periods of time to have a sustained impact on political will, necessitating novel approaches to establish sustained commitment to environmental and climatic risk mitigation efforts. Drawing insights from surveys and innovative machine learning techniques, the research underscores the complexities inherent in achieving effective IEAs and highlights the potential of integrating behavioral economics and collective intelligence to address global environmental challenges.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Beamforming Algorithms for Underwater 2D Acoustical Imaging
abstract: The increasing attention towards underwater acoustic imaging is due to its exceptional ability to produce high-quality images, particularly in challenging and turbid underwater conditions. The heart of any underwater imaging system is beamforming, which is the process of reconstructing the images from the raw hydrophone data. The main focus of this study is on assessing the image quality resulting from different beamforming algorithms, particularly the Delay and Sum (DAS), Delay Multiple and Sum (DMAS), and Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) methods, in the context of underwater acoustic imaging. Qualitative analysis has revealed that the DMAS beamforming algorithm consistently outperforms the others, presenting better lateral resolution and contrast.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic Investigation of a Free Fall Lander for the Descent Trajectory Control
abstract: In this paper we conducted a hydrodynamic investigation of a Free Fall Lander used for ocean explorations. Because such systems do not have any type of control system, we aim to assess drag coefficients and added mass to develop a control strategy based on rudders. The evaluation is conducted by Computational Fluid Dynamics analyses, which in the last years proved to be a useful tool for determining hydrodynamic parameters of AUVs and ROVs. Unlike such systems, Landers are characterized by a much more complex geometry, which makes the analysis more challenging. At first, steady-state and transient analyses are carried out on a simplified version of the Lander (a rectangular cuboid) to confirm the reliability of the simulations, before conducting the same analysis on the Lander's geometry. For the drag coefficient, a further assessment is given by the comparison with the drag force estimated through some of the measurements obtained during the missions in the ocean.

articleTitle: Analysis of Underwater Coral Reef Health Using Neural Networks
abstract: Safeguarding coral reefs requires extensive human effort. Divers, acting as underwater doctors, visually inspect the reefs, demanding expertise and significant resources. Digital methods of coral inspection include taking sequential images or video footage and using the technique of photogrammetry to create benthic maps for expert analysis. While improving scalability, this approach still relies on human interpretation, creating a bottleneck. Advancements in AI, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), offer exciting possibilities. These AI models, deployed on underwater vehicles like ROVs and AUVs, can auto-mate coral detection, classification, and segmentation. However, onboard resource constraints necessitate model optimization for computational efficiency and power consumption. This study showcases the potential of deep neural networks by implementing the YOLOv8 CNN model for automated coral health assessment. The model classifies coral into three cat-egories: healthy, partially bleached, and completely bleached, achieving an accuracy of 78% in validation data. This approach eliminates the need for diversification, significantly enhancing scalability and cost-effectiveness.
