Moreover, deploying the model on underwater vehicles enables real-time monitoring and inter-vention, potentially mitigating damage before it's too late. While promising, further research is crucial. Optimizing the model for even higher accuracy and resource efficiency is essential. Additionally, integrating data from other sensors, such as sonar or LiDAR, could provide a more comprehensive picture of reef health. Ultimately, real-world deployment and validation across diverse coral reef environments will solidify the practical value of AI-powered solutions.

articleTitle: Satellite-Based Sea Surface Prediction and Subsurface Temperature Reconstruction: Integration and Visualization in Open-Source Earth Software
abstract: Underwater temperature profiles hold significant importance in contemporary ocean research and development. There exists a temporal and spatial connection between Sea Surface Temperature (SST) and underwater temperature profiles. Utilizing this spatio-temporal relationship, we propose a predictive reconstruction based on satellite remote sensing data, along with its visualization software. Our model, based on the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), uses historical SST and Sea Level Anomaly (SLA) data from satellite remote sensing to predict the corresponding SST and SLA data for the next ten days. Furthermore, a model combining Empirical Orthogonal Functions (EOF) with a Deep Evidence Regression Network (DERN) utilizes historical underwater temperature profiles and SST information to train a reconstruction model. This establishes a relationship between surface and underwater temperatures. The predicted SST and SLA data for the next ten days, obtained using the prediction model, are used to reconstruct underwater temperature information. The predictive reconstruction module is visualized and integrated into the Earth visualization software, facilitating a more intuitive observation of the global predictive reconstruction results.

articleTitle: Design, Analysis, and Test of a Miniaturized Air-Droppable Underwater Glider
abstract: Underwater gliders are mobile unmanned observation platforms that can observe ocean phenomena (such as turbulence and mesoscale eddies) over an extended period and a wide area at low cost. Nonetheless, Conventional underwater gliders generally require transportation by a mother ship due to their large mass, which may result in significant delays before the designated sea area. Furthermore, research vessels have limited coverage because of their stringent requirements for sea conditions. Hence, this study focuses on the design of an air-droppable underwater glider with improved impact resistance, high maneuverability, and miniaturized design to enable rapid airdrop deployment. This will decrease reliance of underwater gliders on the mother ship and significantly enhance the timeliness of ocean observation, thereby holding significant practical and academic significance.

articleTitle: Countermeasures for Unreliable Inputs and Observations in Multi-AUV Cooperative Localization
abstract: Underwater environments are complex and unpredictable, increasing the possibility of sensor failure. Doppler velocity log (DVL) is an important piece of acoustic equipment, and the location in which it is installed and measurement principles make it vulnerable and unreliable in certain circumstances. Reliable external observations can assist in generating a useful estimate; however, these observations are usually biased due to underwater acoustic communication delays. So in this study, we present a state decoupled delay cubature Kalman filter (SDDCKF) to product useful unknown inputs utilizing observations with delay bias, and obtain accurate posterior estimates of the positions of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). First, the adjustment of delay-induced deviation was executed, and the state space model was reconstructed. Based on this, the state decoupling process was then deduced; and finally, an estimator with improved reliability was designed to handle uncertain input and observations. Results from experiments show that this method breaks the dependence of unknown input estimation on reliable external observation information, and ensures the positioning accuracy of multi-AUV cooperative localization (CL) processes in underwater environments with uncertainty.

articleTitle: Modelling and Analysis of Closed-Loop Depth Control for Underwater Glider - RoBuoy
abstract: Underwater glider (UG) is a unique category of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) having characteristics of low energy consumption and prolonged endurance. These gliders generally employ concept of variable buoyancy for motion. Variable buoyancy results in heave motion and addition of wings to the glider creates a pitching moment due to lift and drag forces acting on the wings. Thus, the heave motion can be converted into horizontal motion achieving three degrees of freedom (DoF) namely surge, heave and pitch. This paper discusses the dynamic modelling of RoBuoy, a novel underwater glider, as presented in [1] which employs the concept of “change of volume” for variable buoyancy. Two linear actuators are connected in a serial configuration to actuate the metallic bellow for changing the volume for the metallic below. Change in stroke length of the linear actuator has its impact both on the buoyancy and pitch angle of the glider. Mathematical modelling involving motor characteristics is crucial to analyze the effect of change in stroke length on the glider parameters and its effect on mission specific parameters. Proposed design parameters of RoBuoy are utilized and dynamic modeling is simulated in MATLAB Simulink environment. A dual loop control methodology is also proposed for depth control of RoBuoy to achieve a trajectory tracking with a maximum permissible error of 0.2 m in zigzag trajectory.

articleTitle: Experimental and Numerical Study of Underwater Acoustic Scattering from Cylinder with Air Cavity
abstract: The scattering of sound waves from a cylinder in free-space is presented. Both experimental measurements and numerical simulation from the cylinder were conducted. The cylinder consists of a steel shell partially filled with concrete. The target strength of this cylinder was obtained at various angles of incidence. The experimental and numerical values agree to a fair extend with differences of up to 5 dB. The difference in target strength at broadside is higher than that when the incident wave is along the cylinder's axis. The target strengths of cylinders complete filled with concrete (no air cavity) and fully concrete cylinder (without steel shell) were also obtained by numerical simulations. It was found that the target strengths are sensitive to the material system of the cylinders, and these may be used as signatures to identify the structural properties of the cylinders.

articleTitle: Acoustic Positioning Enhanced Optical Image Mosaics: A Collaborative Robot-Assisted Approach
abstract: While underwater acoustic imaging devices are im-mune to issues such as turbidity and low visibility, the quality of information that an optical camera provides is richer, if they are in close proximity to an object of interest. Visual inspection is common for large underwater structures such as pipelines, where videos and image mosaics are prepared since individual images may not represent the structure. Current works focus on enhancing individual images and utilizing several techniques to determine features across the sequence of images to stitch them into a mosaic. Given the advances in non-visual sensor-fusion for navigation, dependence of feature-based methods for mosaic generation can be avoided as challenging underwater environments may complicate feature extraction. Therefore, this study aims to generate image mosaics purely utilizing navigation information from a linear Kalman filter (KF), which fuses Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) and SONAR data; a single-beam SONAR attached on an underwater vehicle (UWR) and forward-looking SONAR (FLS) observing the UWR. From experiments, image mosaics were successfully prepared without the use of any feature-based methods, from a distance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1m$</tex> from the target, with the mosaic being about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.5 m$</tex> in width, aided with navigational data from the KF.

articleTitle: Global Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control for Underwater Manipulators Based on Extended State Observer Compensation
abstract: In view of the complexity in modeling the underwater manipulators and the presence of unknown disturbances in practical applications., in this paper., the dynamic model of multi-link underwater manipulators is established by using Lagrange method and considering water resistance., buoyancy and other factors. Building upon this dynamic model., a global fast terminal sliding mode control strategy is designed based on an extended state observer. The observer accurately estimates the disturbances in the system., enabling feedforward compensation for the controller. The convergence of the error equation in finite time is proven using Lyapunov function. Finally., simulations are conducted to compare the proposed algorithm with the traditional sliding mode control based on extended state observer compensation., and the results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithm.

Author Keywords: Global fast terminal sliding mode control

articleTitle: Adaptive neural motion control for a hovercraft subject to dynamic asymmetric constraints
abstract: This paper develops an adaptive neural motion controller for an underactuated hovercraft in the presence of dynamic safety constraints and model uncertainties. Firstly, a surge controller is designed based on an improved asymmetric integral barrier Lyapunov function (AIBLF) to address asymmetric state constraint problems. Secondly, the constraint on the drift angle is transformed into one on the sway speed, and then the virtual sway controller is designed to constrain the sway speed for the purpose of confining the drift angle. Thirdly, a AIBLF is constructed to constrain the yaw angular velocity to inside of safety boundary relating to the surge speed to ensure a safe turning motion at high speed. Neural networks (NNs) are incorporated into each controller to handle the model uncertainties. It is proved that all the tracking errors are ultimately uniformly bounded. Finally, the results from numerous simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control approaches.

articleTitle: Underwater Three-Dimensional Microscope for Marine Benthic Organism Monitoring
abstract: In-situ microscopic imaging of coral reefs or other benthic organisms allows us to monitor how microscale features change in response to the natural environment. However, underwater microscopic imaging remains in its nascent stages, constrained by the complex seafloor environments, and re-quires a more flexible working distance for microscope, a challenge that this paper addresses. In this work, we de-velop an underwater three-dimensional microscope for marine benthic organism monitoring. Specifically, we redesigned the optical path structure of the microscope by incorporating an electrically tunable lens, enabling dynamic adjustment of the working distance. This allows each scan of the microscope to produce an image stack rather than a single image, which contains different views of the specimen at each focus plane change. We then use image fusion algorithms to generate a fully clear image and a 3D model from the image stack. The proposed microscope enables long-term, in-situ, real-time monitoring of benthic marine environments, providing researchers with micrometer-resolution, clear, high-quality 2D and 3D image data of microbenthos and meiobenthos.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Ship Propeller Noise Conducted in a Test Tank
abstract: As one of the dominant noise components on ships, studies on propeller noise still need to be carried out. Both numerical and experimental techniques are continuing to develop, to obtain noise that is caused by cavitation of the propeller. Restrictive noise at sea, especially that caused by ships, has become a widely discussed issue because it will affect marine life. Based on this background, a study on propeller cavitation noise was conducted by conducting experiments in the towing tank of the Indonesia National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN). A B3-35 propeller model and an electric motor connected to a vertical shaft were used for this experiment. Variations in propeller rotation speed were made to generate cavitation around the propeller. The generated propeller cavitation noise signal was analyzed in the frequency domain by studying the generated spectrum. An underwater camera was used to observe the cavitation phenomena underwater. From the results of this experiment, it is found that the higher the propeller rotation speed, the greater the cavitation that appears. The resulting spectrum also shows that if the noise is recorded at a considerable distance, more frequency components will be obtained.

articleTitle: Bioindication Complex Based on Underwater Digital Holography
abstract: The paper presents methods of obtaining information on the ecological well-being of the ecosystem based on the results of plankton in situ monitoring. It describes a bioindication complex based on a submersible digital holographic camera (DHC), which is used to obtain the monitoring series of measurements of selected parameters both for the natural and photostimulated state of plankton. The spectral analysis of these series was used to determine the rhythms of plankton activity. It is shown that the stability of rhythmic processes of plankton concentration change in the DHC working volume can be used as a marker of disturbance of the ecosystem well-being. The paper presents the results of a field digital holographic experiment for the biotesting of water areas in high latitudes and methods of interpreting data characterizing the behavioral activity of plankton in habitat.

articleTitle: A Sustainable Energy Mix for Small Islands in the Pacific Oceans. The Case Study of Vanuatu
abstract: The installation of technologies supplied by Renewable Energy Sources is mandatory to improve the environmental sustainability and loosen the dependence on fossil fuels. Furthermore, the energy transition can strengthen the stability of the energy market, especially in small islands. At the same time, the need for large infrastructure construction could be alleviated in developing areas. In this context, the proposed paper analyzes the current scenario of the small developing countries of the Pacific Ocean. In particular, the case study of Vanuatu is assessed, analyzing the available renewable energy sources: solar, wind and sea wave.

articleTitle: Innovative Design of a Submersible Multimode High-Speed Unmanned Surface Vehicle
abstract: In this paper, a submersible multimode high-speed unmanned surface vehicle (USV) is studied. Firstly, the type design and general layout design of the USV are introduced, and then the sailing performance of the USV is simulated and analyzed. Importantly, according to the multi-modal characteristics of the USV, a repeatable submersible system is designed, and the repeatable surfacing and diving modes are studied. Finally, the control system of the USV is studied and designed. The experimental results show that the USV has the characteristics of high speed and flexible maneuverability, which has certain practical value.

articleTitle: Study on the Physical Changes of Structure I Methane Hydrate under External Forces
abstract: The ocean, continental shelf, and permafrost are abundant in CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> hydrates, rendering them highly promising sources of clean energy. The mechanical stability of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> hydrate plays a crucial role in their extraction and storage. Being solid in nature, external forces, such as earthquakes, can induce physical damage to CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> hydrates. This study employs the molecular dynamics method to simulate the uniaxial-deformation behavior of structure I (sI type) CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> hydrate under stress. Irrespective of the application of either stretch or squeeze force, alterations in the physical parameters were observed, encompassing variations in the count of hydrate cages, order parameters, and the quantity of water molecules in both the liquid and solid phases. It was ascertained that upon complete separation of the hydrate, the stress promptly reverts to a value of about 0 GPa. During the process of squeezing, the stress remains non-zero as a result of continuous contact between the solid and liquid phases. When the hydrate is subjected to stretching, approximately 5% of water molecules undergo a phase transition from solid to liquid, while approximately 8% of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> molecules lose their encapsulation and become free. Conversely, during the compression phase, the larger cages (5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) are more susceptible to deformation compared to the smaller cages (5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>). Ultimately, nearly all of the larger cages and 92% of the smaller cages are crushed, leading to the liberation of approximately 97.6% of the CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> from the cages. This significant release of CH4 presents a potential security concern.

articleTitle: Arctic Sea Temperature Data: Comparative Decomposition Analysis With EEMD, CEEMDAN & VMD
abstract: Evaluating components of environmental time series, such as diurnals, seasonal and trends of Arctic Sea water temperatures are key to providing an understanding of any pattern shifts in such a sensitive environment. This analysis requires a robust decomposition method, given the challenges posed by the presence of noisy, missing, non-stationary and nonlinear signal characteristics. Traditional frequency analysis techniques, such as Fourier techniques, are compromised in the context of these data types. Two variants of the Empirical Mode Decomposition method and a Variational Mode Decomposition technique are comparatively assessed as prime candidates, given the data context. A baseline application of the three techniques to a synthesised signal is established, followed by direct application to an annual sea water temperature dataset from the Gascoyne Bay inlet in the Arctic.

articleTitle: Comparing Different YOLO Versions for Boat Detection and Classification in Real Datasets
abstract: Boat detection and classification is extremely im-portant for tasks such as autonomous navigation of unmanned vessels with collision avoidance or target identification (maritime security). Most popular approaches use deep learning and in particular the You-Only-Look-Once (YOLO) algorithm. YOLO has had a tremendous development and nowadays many different versions are available. This paper focus on testing and evaluating the most recent YOLO versions found in the state of the art in the context of boat detection and classification. Results show that while YOLO v8 may not have the highest precision it does provide overall the best results.

Index Terms: Version Of You Only Look Once

articleTitle: Design and Experiments of a Sustainable Hybrid Power Unmanned Surface Vehicle for Maritime Patrol
abstract: This study presents the development of the Ark of Dream, an innovative hybrid power unmanned surface vehicle (USV) specifically designed for sustainable maritime patrol. This USV is uniquely outfitted with a combination of sail and water-jet propulsion systems, supplemented by a solar power system for generating electricity. These features enable the USV to sustain prolonged daily patrols and enhance its capability for quick responses in emergency scenarios. Additionally, the USV is equipped with advanced autonomous operation technologies, including sophisticated sensors, communication and navigation devices, and intelligent control algorithms. To assess its practicality, comprehensive sea trials have been conducted, testing the USV's performance under different propulsion modes. The study also explores the application of Line-of-Sight (LOS) and Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) algorithms for guiding and controlling the USV's motion, with the results demonstrating effective performance to follow the predetermined path in real sea.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of INS coarse alignment methods in real drift conditions
abstract: The initial alignment stage of inertial navigation systems (INS) is of paramount importance for strategic vehicular applications. Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), for instance, are an example of vehicles whose navigation relies on such systems. One of the main encumbrances of the AUV alignment stage lies of the fact that it is usually conducted in open sea conditions, wherein the wave and wind disturbances impair the attainment of the applicable accuracy and convergence time requirements. This work addresses the aforementioned problem by presenting a comparative evaluation of the well-known attitude decomposition-based initial alignment (ADIA), based on different vector observation approaches. As main contribution of the work, we show that the non-optimized version of ADIA based on unaided observations of acceleration integrals (I-DVA) equates, in terms of accuracy and convergence time, to more sophisticated (aided and/or optimized) ADIA approaches, being able to deliver heading angle estimates accurate to $1.0-1.5$ degrees for alignment times beyond 100 seconds. Results from experimental tests are conducted with an autonomous surface vehicle (ASV) in real drift conditions, which confirm the outlined verifications.

articleTitle: Incipient Fault Analysis of Thruster Propellers from Offshore Operations
abstract: A crucial component for unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs), including remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), are the thrusters, which, in addition, are sensitive to damage during operations in harsh environments. This paper presents a study on the impact of incipient faults on the performance of thruster propellers used in offshore operations. The study evaluates the reduction in propeller performance due to wear and tear under realistic working conditions. The study employs a combination of experimental data analysis and signal processing techniques, including fast Fourier transforms and harmonics analysis, to identify faults and assess their severity. The results show that worn propellers can be identified through 5th-order harmonics and rotational velocity changes. The paper concludes with a proposal for future research using a model-based approach to enhance fault detection capabilities further.

articleTitle: Underwater Data Mule Communication Between Autonomous Underwater Vehicle and Seafloor Platform
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) can be used for data mule communications to retrieve data collected by sensor platforms placed on the seafloor and upload it to the surface with the help of underwater wireless optical communication. We propose a reinforcement learning-based control strategy for maneuvering AUV to approach the seafloor platform and establish a communication link to collect data. The trained controller was tested in a simulated environment, and the maximum pointing error was maintained at about 1 meter. In the future, the proposed data mule communication will be deployed in actual machine experiments.

articleTitle: Technology Requirements for Monitoring Reporting and Verification of Ocean Carbon Dioxide Removal
abstract: This paper analyzes the need for new technologies to support monitoring reporting and verification (MRV) solutions for ocean carbon dioxide removal (oCDR). Current scientific, investment, and policy considerations suggest that to mitigate climate change it will be necessary to utilize the ocean as a resource in removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. The latest IPCC report notes that limiting warming to 1.5C will require around 6 GtC02 of CDR per year by 2050. In 2021 the US National Academy of Science and Engineering released a report describing the underlying concepts of oCDR. While these techniques vary they share one common consideration. All oCDR approaches will depend upon effective MRV to validate that carbon is sequestered. This “trust” is fundamental to the future economy of oCDR founded upon scientific credibility and social license. While oCDR MRV will draw upon advances in modeling it will also depend upon in situ monitoring. In all likelihood, the number of in situ bio-geochemical measurements required to support global MRV will be two, or possibly four, orders of magnitude more than the most extensive ocean measurements conducted today. This paper summarizes oCDR concepts. It goes on to examine the current state-of-the art in solutions for oCDR MRV and reviews development in ocean observing platforms and emerging ocean carbon sensors. Combining these analyses, this paper evaluates trends in sensor and platform economics to anticipate a likely oCDR MRV system solution that will be commercially viable in the next five to ten years.

articleTitle: Achieving Time Diversity by Using Packet-Repetition Based Scheme in Translational Acoustic-RF Channels
abstract: Recently, cross-medium communication combining acoustic wave and millimeter wave has gained more and more attention because it provides a direct communication method from underwater to above water without the need for relays. Presently, the feasibility of this method in short-distance communication has been verified. However, when extending to long-distance communication, the reduction in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) due to the attenuation of sound and electromagnetic waves will present a challenge to the performance of communication. This paper proposes a packet-repetition-based scheme to achieve time diversity. Experimental results demonstrate that the pro-posed scheme effectively reduces the average bit error rate in translational acoustic-radio frequency channels.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Influence of Bow Shape on Gliding Motion and Water-Entry Impact Force of an Airdropped Underwater Glider
abstract: The air-dropped underwater gliders have the advantage in deployment efficiency and deployment range. The bow shape has effect on both hydrodynamic force and water-entry impact force. Therefore, it is necessary to comprehensively consider the effects of water-entry impact force and motion performance on the bow shape designing of an air-dropped underwater glider. In this paper, the influence of bow shape on hydrodynamic performance and water-entry impact force are numerical studied. The results show that the smaller the bow hemisphere angle, the smaller the drag force and the water-entry impact force. The conclusions can provide a reference for the designing of bow shape of air-dropped underwater glider.

articleTitle: Enhancing Image Quality Assessment Using CNN-Based Edge Detection
abstract: Underwater survey applications suffer from ma-jor image degradation. Many times there is major image degradation from attenuation, scattering and dispersion. This can significantly impact the ability of algorithms to extract meaningful information from the data. This work presents an objective metric that assesses the quality of the images obtained by the camera, thus providing a measurement that can be used to monitor and track the quality of the input images. The proposed algorithm leverages existing metrics, and by adding a light weight CNN-based edge detection, is able to significantly improve the metric performance for quantifying the perceptual quality of underwater images.

articleTitle: eDNA Survey in the Arctic with an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle
abstract: The eDNA autonomous biosampler results from a line of research aimed at developing systems for sampling and collecting marine biological data, and for collecting environmen-tal DNA. Environmental DNA is a tool that has been increasingly used in the biological monitoring of aquatic environments, as it is a non-invasive method with very promising results when it comes to assessing biological diversity. In this sense, the automation of this method has the potential to greatly increase the temporal and spatial resolution of current biological monitoring programs in aquatic environments. The system has been developed in a partnership between research teams at the Centre for Robotics and Autonomous Systems (CRAS - INESC TEC) and CIIMAR and has been tested in multiple operational scenarios, including the Arctic, where it was attached to the AUV IRIS.

articleTitle: Application of Blue Whale wave gliders in nearshore areas
abstract: Wave gliders are relatively inexpensive, lightweight craft for sea-surface studies and are widely used in oceanography. In this study, observations in Daya Bay, China were conducted using Blue Whale wave gliders from July 21 to 29, 2019. The virtual anchoring operation model of the wave glider was selected to validate the fixed-point observation functionality of the glider, and the results showed that more than 93% of the time points were within a radius of 0.5 km. The weather and wave data observed by the wave gliders were similar to the data observed by offshore buoys. Using a temperature chain installed beneath the wave glider and extending beneath the sea surface, the summertime cold-water intrusion extending along the bottom from the northern South China Sea into Daya Bay was validated. Extension of the cold-water intrusion toward the surface of the bay was suppressed by the momentum flux injected by the surface wind, indicating that a larger wind response results in a thinner layer of cold bottom water. This new observation method based on using a temperature chain beneath a wave glider can be applied to observe coastal phenomena with fine temporal resolution, expanding the potential applications of wave gliders.

articleTitle: Acoustic Field Fluctuation of Source-Generated Internal Waves and a Robust Detection Method
abstract: When a submerged target travels through density-stratified water between bistatic sonar, the source-generated internal waves will disturb the background acoustic channel, making target detection possible. In this paper, three-dimensional amplitude field of source-generated internal wave was constructed based on model of sphere target, and fluctuation of transmission sound field was developed. Characteristics of internal wave on different crossing angles and traveling time were simulated, and the inverse proportional relationship between channel fluctuation and crossing angle was revealed. In order to overcome the overshadow effect of background sound field, a detection method based on empirical orthogonal function was developed to extract the weak distortion characteristics. A lake experiment was conducted to demonstrate the ability.

articleTitle: Developing a Marine Energy Workforce Pipeline through STEM Education
abstract: Marine Energy is a nascent but growing industry and will need a strong workforce to be successful. This paper examines the resources and programs needed to achieve the industry's goals.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of New Modulation Technique, OTSM, in Underwater Acoustic Channel
abstract: The orthogonal time sequencey multiplexing (OTSM) scheme is a newly proposed modulation scheme for 6G wireless communication system that uses the Walsh Hadamard transform (WHT) with lower complexity than the Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS). There is a considerable literature survey for the OTFS modulation scheme in the underwater channel, but the OTSM modulation technique has not been tested in the underwater channel. So, this work considers analyzing the performance of the OTSM scheme in the underwater channel with the complex Gaussian noise using single tap time and single tap time-frequency domain MMSE equalization. We then evaluate the comparison performance in terms of the bit error rate of the OTSM with the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) and OTFS based underwater systems using these equalizations. We noticed that the OTSM-based UWAC performs better with the time domain single tap MMSE equalizer and gives almost the same as the OTFS scheme but at much lower computational complexity and outperforms OFDM in both domains.

articleTitle: Investigation of Three-Dimensional Sound Field Horizontal Refraction in Heterogeneous Topography
abstract: The variability in seafloor topography is a primary factor influencing sound propagation. Complex and varied seabed topographies generate differing degrees of sound propagation effects, thereby altering the sound propagation loss compared to a flat seabed. This paper analyzes and statistically processes the slope data of the selected area's terrain. It utilizes acoustic models to simulate and compare the sound propagation loss in convergence zones and near the deep-sea sound channel axis under different slope conditions. The findings indicate that an upslope terrain reduces propagation loss in convergence zones, and the propagation loss is minimized near the deep-sea sound channel axis when the downslope gradient is 7°. The paper also examines and discusses the impact of different bottom sediment parameters on sound propagation loss and the backscattering of acoustic energy in upslope conditions. Finally, the study analyzes the horizontal refraction effect in the three-dimensional sound field under complex terrain conditions from ray trajectories perspective.

articleTitle: Target Detection in Clutter Regions Based on 3DCNN for HFSWR
abstract: High-frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) has the characteristics of low power consumption and all-weather operation, and plays an irreplaceable role in maritime target detection tasks. However, vessel targets are often submerged in sea clutter, which leads to a significant reduction in the detection accuracy of traditional detection algorithms. In this paper, a two-stage target detection algorithm in sea clutter is proposed. The proposed method includes pre-processing stage and detection stage. In the pre-processing stage, the range-Doppler spectrum is expanded to direction-range-Doppler three-dimensional (3D) spectrum by digital beam forming (DBF) method, and then the extremum detector is used to perform sliding window detection in the 3D spectrum to obtain the 3D tensor blocks of suspicious target regions. In detection stage the designed 3D convolutional neural network (3DCNN) is used to extract spatial features from the suspicious 3D tensor blocks and input them into the fully connected layer for binary classification. Experiments show that the detection performance of the proposed algorithm in the sea clutter is significantly better than the traditional detection algorithms.

articleTitle: Non-Binary Polar Coded Continuous Phase Modulation for Underwater Acoustic Communication
abstract: Conventional underwater acoustic communication (UAC) systems typically employ a direct cascading approach of channel coding and continuous phase modulation (CPM). Although this approach has shown inspiring performance, the detection and the decoding processes are treated as separate modules, which results in incompletely exploiting the state information of CPM. We propose an improved joint detection and decoding scheme for non-binary CPM and polar codes. Furthermore, considering the exponential complexity growth of CPM with modulation order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> and memory length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>, a complexity reduction strategy is proposed to enhance practicality. Through simulations, we have validated the reliability of the proposed joint scheme, which exhibits significant performance improvements compared to traditional strategies of separate detection and decoding.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation of Forward-Looking Sonar Images Based on Improved Deeplabv3+
abstract: The deep-learning segmentation algorithms of forward-looking sonar (FLS) image could effectively assist underwater vehicles in the task of searching for underwater targets. However, a large number of non-target highlights in FLS image due to the acoustic imaging principle bring great challenges for segmentation. In this paper, a novel semantic segmentation network with multi-level feature fusion capability to overcome these challenges is proposed. We adopt DeepLabv3+ with encoder-decoder architecture as the main framework. In addition, we integrate a newly feature fusion module (FFM) and attention in decoder. We have carried out a series of experiments on the self-made FLS dataset. Experimental results demonstrate the superior segmentation performance of this method over other methods on the complex region of FLS image where non-target highlights and target highlights are fused.

articleTitle: Experimental Deployment of Automatic Buoy Identification Monitoring System (ABIMS) for Sustainable Fishery and Healthy Oceans
abstract: Recent advancements in the collaboration between Marine Technology and 4IR Information Technology have led to the development of the Automatic Buoy Identification Monitoring System (ABIMS) in Korea. ABIMS utilizes location tracking, location message communication, machine learning, and data analytics, to monitor fishing buoys and report abnormal behaviors of connected fishing gears, in real-time, addressing the issue of abandoned, lost, or discarded (ALD) fishing gears. This system contributes to sustainable fisheries management and healthier oceans by effectively tracking gear movement, detecting loss or abandonment, and informing evidence-based decision-making for various unexpected happening events related to fishing gears under monitoring. Korea's efforts with the newly developed and experimented ABIMS are expected to minimize the impact of ALD fishing gears and promote sustainable fishing practices.

articleTitle: Spatial Undersampling SAS Imaging Algorithm Utilizes Dual Carrier Frequency Azimuth Compressed Sensing
abstract: Restricted by factors such as sonar carrier size, carrier velocity, underwater sound velocity and sound propagation characteristics, there are certain limitations in the mapping efficiency of synthetic aperture sonar(SAS). Spatial undersampling occurs in the azimuth when the moving speed of SAS is too high, resulting in grating lobe, pseudo-targets and blurred imaging azimuths. To address this problem, this paper proposes a spatial undersampling SAS imaging algorithm based on dual carrier frequency azimuth compressed sensing, the algorithm introduces the scene sparse a priori information in azimuth, transmits dual carrier frequency signals, and improves the traditional range doppler(RD) algorithm based on the theory of compressed sensing, which achieves a better undersampling imaging. Then, the grating lobe and pseudo target caused by high-speed undersampling is further suppressed by using the property that the position of the grating lobe is related to the carrier frequency. The simulated imaging results and experiments show that when the mapping speed exceeds the theoretical limit speed of SAS, i.e., when there is serious spatial undersampling in azimuth, the proposed algorithm still achieves high-resolution imaging, effectively suppresses the grating lobe and pseudo targets caused by the undersampling, and greatly improves the mapping efficiency.

articleTitle: Fine-Tuning Neural Network Based Target Localization Using Sources of Opportunity
abstract: In addressing the practical challenges of underwater localization using deep learning, the acquisition of a significant amount of real-world data proves essential yet challenging. Motivated by the available dataset from opportunistic ships in the ocean, this paper proposes source localization through a combination of simulated data, measured data from opportunistic sources, and very limited deployed underwater sources. The methodology commences with the pre-training of RDL-CNN (Range Depth Learning - Convolutional Neural Networks), using only the simulated data. Subsequently, Transfer Learning (TL) is introduced, denoted as the RDL-CNN-TL model, which fine-tunes RDL-CNN using a limited dataset from the actual environment. Results demonstrate that even in mismatched environments, the proposed RDL-CNN-TL model, utilizing data from two depths (opportunistic surface ships and limited deployed sources), can accurately estimate the source range and discerns the source depth across the water column.

articleTitle: Robotic Field Experiments for Critical Infrastructure Protection in the REPMUS 2023 Military Exercise
abstract: This paper presents the results of field trials performed with the EVA autonomous underwater vehicle in the protection of critical infrastructures. The trials were conducted in the context of the REPMUS23 naval exercise organized by the Portuguese Navy. EVA was successfully deployed in a mission of detailed inspection of a submarine cable and in the detection and localization of a possible hostile attack with explosive charges. Multibeam sonar and structured laser light systems were also used to locate and obtain a detailed model of the TURTLE robotic lander deployed on the sea bottom.

articleTitle: Development of a triboelectric nanogenerator toward self-powered ocean observatory
abstract: Autonomous underwater mobile platforms usually rely on cables or batteries for energy supply, which has the problem of limited energy supply, which is not conducive to the development of distributed marine sensing networks. Here, we designed a hydrostatic pressure energy harvesting triboelectric nanogenerator (HP-TENG) for harvesting the energy of the hydrostatic pressure difference in the ocean to power the underwater equipment. HP-TENG’s spiral shaft drive design and TENG module can convert differential pressure energy into mechanical energy and further into electrical energy. The HP-TENG can generate an output current of $4.41 \ \mu \mathrm{A}$ and an open-circuit voltage of 26.1 V at a compression speed of $4 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$, and the total power output in a single compression process can be significantly increased by changing the spiral angle of the shaft. In addition, the power generated by the HP-TENG can also power low-power devices, and the generated energy at a compression speed of 2 $\mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{s}$ can be rectified to successfully light up 20 commercial LEDs. The results hold prospects for underwater blue energy harvesting and are expected to contribute to the development of self-powered equipment toward emerging “smart ocean” and blue economy applications.

articleTitle: Passive Acoustic Environment in Kao-Ping Submarine Canyon at the Southwest of Taiwan
abstract: The Kao-Ping Submarine Canyon (KPSC) located in southwest Taiwan which has abundant shellfish supporting nearby fishing activities at Donggang township. There are ferries en route to and from Liuqui island, mostly for tourist activities. The submarine canyon traps suspended fine-grained sediments morphologically with episodic large river discharges after intensive rainfall triggered by tropical storms. Various biophony, geophony, and anthrophony sound sources make it a unique location for studying the acoustic environment in the submarine canyon. We deployed a subsurface mooring equipped with a passive acoustic array, Acoustic Doppler Current Profilers (ADCPs), Conductivity-Temperature-Depth (CTD) sensor, and turbidity sensors at the depth $\sim 350$ meters along the thalweg line for a period of three weeks. The acoustic array comprises four hydrophones configured as a vertical line array. Each hydrophone is precisely spaced 30 cm apart with a sampling rate of 64 kHz. The ancillary data collected includes meteorological data from a surface buoy nearby. Acoustic array data is analyzed using an unsupervised machine learning program. Utilizing cluster analysis, the audio data is grouped into distinct regions characterized by either high or low frequencies. Preliminary findings indicate that the ambient noise spectrum is primarily dominated by episodic ferry noises throughout the day. During the night, the acoustic spectra in the low-frequency band ($\lt 3 \mathbf{k H z}$) shift to biological sources. Detecting and classifying other geophony sources such as wind, rain, and hyperpycnal flows prove to be challenging due to the dominance of strong anthropogenic sources in the region. A detailed statistical description of the ambient noise content will be presented based on the data collected.

articleTitle: Ocean Noise Field-Calibration Constraints for Deep Sea Mining
abstract: The EU Horizon project TRIDENT aims at developing a comprehensive study to improve the understanding of the activities related to deep sea mining as well as to develop observation methodologies, technologies required for impact forecast, and possible mitigation measures. In the framework of TRIDENT, the impact of the acoustic field will be assessed by deploying a fixed array of acoustic recorders in the surrounding of the mining activity on top of the Tropic Seamount to monitor the near field, while acoustic gliders equipped with hydrophones will provide the observations from the far field. In complement, noise models will be routinely used for predicting sound distribution requiring frequent calibration with field data with a suitable spatial coverage. This work proposes a methodology and tests the calibration capabilities for ocean noise modelling in the context of DSM activities, where the main objective is to define the best sampling strategy for a glider to record data for calibrating acoustic propagation models. The analysis of the broadband transmission loss from contrasting oceanographic conditions allowed the identification of regions of interest assuring the best use of the acoustic glider in the upcoming sea trial.

articleTitle: Cross-Medium Communication Combining Infrared Optical and Acoustic Waves
abstract: In recent years, direct communication across the water-air interface without relay has become possible by combining acoustic and millimetre waves. Present cross-medium communication schemes combining acoustic and electromagnetic waves are carried out in three steps. First, the underwater transducer sends acoustic waves, and the waves hit the water surface and induce vibrations. Then, a millimeter-wave radar in the air sends electromagnetic waves to detect the water surface vibrations. Last, after processing the received signals from the radar, cross-medium communication is achieved. However, this scheme suffers from short communication distances (approximately 1 m over water) and low resolution (millimetre level). Laser Doppler Vibrometry (LDV) is superior with high resolution and long measuring distances. Therefore, for the first time, we creatively adopted infrared LDV instead of millimeter-wave radar. This new approach improves the communication distance and distance resolution and achieves cross-medium communication with 10.8 m above water and 3.5 m underwater. In this article, we reveal the transmission mechanism of cross-medium communication combining infrared and acoustic waves and use experiments to preliminarily verify the feasibility of this scheme. In our experiments, we evaluate the effects of the depth and carrier frequency of the transmitted acoustic wave signals as well as the height of the receiving end on cross-medium communication.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation and Experimental Research on an Underwater Dredging Robot
abstract: The paper studies underwater dredging robots for wall cleaning in long-distance water conveyance tunnels. Limnoperna fortunei and other organisms will adhere to water conveyance tunnel walls after a prolonged use, affecting the water's quality. An underwater dredging robot was designed inside the tunnel walls to remove these organisms. The paper proposes a novel mechanical structure for underwater dredging. A detailed description of the machinery and control system of the working section is provided. Tests in actual pool experiments and simulations of nozzles demonstrated that the underwater dredging robot could effectively clean the adsorbed Limnoperna fortune.

articleTitle: TGFish: A Temporal Graph Convolutional Network for Fishing Effort Distribution Prediction
abstract: Predicting the distribution of fishing effort is essential for effective fisheries management, allowing for the creation of fishing plans and the preservation of marine biological resources. However, this prediction faces three main challenges: the unquantified impact of hydrological factors on fishing effort distribution, as well as the spatial and temporal patterns of fishing vessel behavior. In this study, we aim to measure the correlation between hydrological factor fields and fishing effort distribution. From this analysis, we propose a system called TGFish, which can predict day-to-day fishing effort distribution for the upcoming week. TGFish integrates graph convolution neural networks to extract features from fishing effort distribution and hydrological factor fields, addressing spatial constraints, and LSTM to handle temporal constraints. We use the VMS dataset from 1,899 trawling fishing vessels in the East China Sea between September 2015 and May 2017. The dataset from September 2015 to May 2016 is used for correlation analysis and model training, while the dataset from September 2016 to May 2017 is employed to evaluate prediction accuracy. Extensive experimentation demonstrates that TGFish effectively predicts the day-level distribution of fishing effort for the upcoming week. The results confirm the effectiveness and reliability of our proposed system.

articleTitle: Design of Water-Ice Amphibious Vehicle for Under-Ice Observation
abstract: The exploration and study of polar oceans are crucial concerns for scientists. The unique environment of polar oceans and the specific observational requirements pose special challenges for conventional underwater robots. Amphibious robots, capable of adapting to the complex and dynamic polar environment, are particularly suitable. Hence, this paper pri-marily focuses on the design of a water-ice amphibious vehicle. Driven by propellers and ice-spur wheels, the vehicle is capable of surface navigation, under-ice navigation, and crossing ice layers. Additionally, the paper introduces a vision-based light source-guided recovery system to enhance the vehicle's autonomy during under-ice exploration. Experimental tests were conducted on a frozen lake and in controlled pool environments, providing initial verification of the vehicle's proficiency in surface navigation, under-ice exploration, and successful traversal of ice layers. Furthermore, under limited conditions on land, the preliminary tests of the light source-guided recovery system demonstrated its feasibility for short-distance recovery.

articleTitle: Propeller Hydrodynamic Performance Optimization Based on Deep Learning
abstract: In order to achieve efficient optimization of propeller hydrodynamic performance and overcome the shortcomings of traditional optimization methods that rely too much on experience to achieve theoretical optimal design, a propeller hydrodynamic performance optimization method based on deep learning and the Dynamic Adaptive Beetle Swarm Antennae Search algorithm is proposed in this article. The propeller hydrodynamic performance prediction model consists of multiple inception module based on separable convolution and residual connection; the new algorithm: DABSAS is proposed to optimize the hydrodynamic performance by adjusting its geometric parameters within a certain interval. The KP505 is taken as the experiment object to test the optimization method, the results of it show that the efficiency of KP505 is increased by up to 5.4% after optimization which verifies the validity of the DABSAS; the accuracy of the prediction model is basically the same as that of CFD method and the calculation cycle is extremely short, which can know the open water performance of the propeller in realtime and avoid multiple model tests to save costs.

Author Keywords: dynamic adaptive beetle swarm antennae search algorithm

articleTitle: LOTUS: Learning from Operational Teaming with Unmanned Systems
abstract: The LOTUS project aims at improving maritime surveillance. In this context, this position paper presents ongoing contributions, including novel machine learning algorithms for multi-agent systems to be applied to groups of underwater drones involved in surveillance missions. It emphasises incorporating human-machine teaming to bolster decision-making in maritime scenarios. The expected outcomes of this project comprise the robust control of groups of autonomous vehicles, adaptable to environmental changes, as well as an effective reporting method. Mission summaries will be delivered to human operators by way of narratives about the relevant events detected thanks to drones. The integration of this narrative construction powered by machine learning will enhance the overall effectiveness of the team, constituting a significant breakthrough.

articleTitle: Breaking the Waves: A Region-Based Feature Matching Method in Wave Images Using Improved Coherent Point Drift
abstract: The homogeneity and adequacy of keypoint matching are critical to visual measurement of sea waves. However, the sparsely distributed edges and corners in weakly textured scenarios of wave images, can lead to a lack of abundant feature points, which gives rise to an insufficiency of distinct descriptors that can effectively discriminate between different keypoints. In this paper, we proposed a region-Based feature matching method in wave images using improved Coherent Point Drift (CPD). The process begins with segmenting the wave image into superpixels. Landmark-superpixels are then located using a certain keypoint matching method. These superpixels are crucial in identifying regions with weak textures, assessed by their relative locations, and the identified regions also serve to correspond to the region in stereo pairs. Point set registration is executed for points within the regions. In the matching stage, a matrix form of constraint terms is employed, aimed at ensuring motion consistency across the aggregation of the superpixel. This is complemented by a non-rigid transform model, which plays a pivotal role in directing the registration process. Our motivation is to avoid ambiguities introduced by feature descriptors during the matching process and to limit the distortion of point set alignment by utilizing region-based and locally consistent alignment strategies. Experimental results show that the method successfully matches significantly more keypoints and has the best uniformity performance compared to the comparison methods. The method achieves a more competitive performance in terms of both visual quality and objective assessment compared to other classical feature matching methods and deep learning-based methods.

articleTitle: Hydrodynamic Performance of an Oscillating Water Column with Inclined Walls and a Submerged Plate: A Numerical Study.
abstract: This study aims to improve the efficiency of the OWC by integrating it with inclined walls and a submerged horizontal plate. This integration is designed to increase the wave height near the device, resulting in a more effective energy extraction. To achieve this, a flat square plate was used, and an OWC with inclined walls was installed. A numerical study was conducted using open-source CFD software to investigate the efficiency of OWC by measuring the air pressure and wave elevation inside the chamber. The model is validated by comparing the numerical results with experimental data. The test was conducted at a constant water depth of 0.5 m, involving a fixed horizontal plate positioned at 0.3 m below the still water level. The model, with and without the flat square plate at the same level, was subjected to regular waves with periods ranging from 0.8 s to 2 s, maintaining a consistent wave height of 0.05 m. The results show that the integration of OWC with harbor walls with a submerged plate increases efficiency compared to the absence of a plate.

articleTitle: Simulator for Underwater Acoustic Vector Sensor's Recorded Pressure and Particle Velocity Signals for User Defined Scenarios
abstract: This paper presents a simulator for pressure and particle velocity signals recorded by an underwater Acoustic Vector Sensor (AVS) for user-defined scenarios, incorporating an underwater sound propagation model to estimate the AVS's signals. Its utility is multi-fold. Firstly, it can be used to study and evaluate the performance of signal processing algorithms such as DOA estimation for various underwater applications. Secondly, it acts as a precursor or substitute for a controlled testing environment during the prototyping phase. The AVS consists of one hydrophone and three co-located orthogonal uniaxial accelerometers, effectively encoding the sound field's 4D information. It measures acoustic pressure and particle velocity along three orthogonal axes. It inherently exhibits a directivity index of 3–6 dB compared to a hydrophone. Compared to hydrophone arrays, its dimensions are significantly smaller. These qualities make it a better option than hydrophone arrays when looking for compact, directed acoustic receivers for applications like AUV platforms. Thus, this paper has addressed the need for an AVS simulator in order to better understand and design supporting algorithms. The presented simulator may serve multiple user defined scenarios. For a given input pressure waveform, it emulates the signals received at the four channels of the AVS in both physical and electrical units. Furthermore, the validity of the simulated signals is verified through separate analyses using cases independent of the simulator.

articleTitle: Sand Textual Distribution on Cross-Shore Slope at Gyungpo Beach in Korea
abstract: The cross-shore slope represents an active portion of a shoreline, where wave run-up and run-down flow interactions occur with a littoral zone. The sand size is a significant variable when predicting beach morphology changes related to coastal erosion. However, there is a lack of information about sand size, sorting, skewness, and cross-shore slope on Gyungpo Beach, which is located in the eastern area of South Korea, for an understanding of its coastal environment. In this paper, the relationship between mean grain size and cross-shore slope has been investigated. In order to obtain accurate estimates of sand size parameters, sand samples were taken from the target beach using the traditional sieving method. The beach profile data, including the cross-shore slope, were collected using a VRS GNSS system mounted on a quad bike or on a surveyor’s backpack. Several field data acquisition campaigns were conducted over a period of nine years.

articleTitle: HF Coastal Ocean Radar for Sustainable Development
abstract: Surface current maps from a phased array HF radar are produced continuously at 15-minute intervals. This enables calculation of time-resolved divergence and curl parameters to identify dynamical features of a river plume. Lagrangian tracking through a tidal cycle is used to follow the paths of virtual drifters in the low salinity water. The HF radar product serves to integrate the features of in situ sampling and satellite SAR imagery.

articleTitle: A Study on the Algorithm for Measuring Sea Fog Intensity Using Real Sea Images and Its Performance Verification
abstract: Many accidents at sea are caused by low visibility due to sea fog, making it essential to estimate the intensity and visibility of sea fog in real time in the marine environment. However, existing estimation systems are costly, rendering them impractical for installation in various locations, such as small vessels, minor ports, and numerous buoys. Consequently, this paper proposes an algorithm known as RDCP (Reduced Dark Channel Prior), which provides low-complexity, cost-effective estimations. To perform the estimation, the RDCP algorithm initially acquires dark channels from an ocean image, then applies an optimized threshold value to these channels and removes the sky region from the ocean image. For evaluating the estimation performance, 640 original images captured from cameras at four different ports in South Korea were used, instead of artificially composed images. Considering the power-limited operating environments typical of marine facilities, the processing time performance of the RDCP algorithm was also examined. The experimental results demonstrate that the RDCP algorithm provides reliable estimation performance in realtime.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Order Variation Mathematical Modeling of Ship Maneuvering Motion Under Environmental Changes
abstract: The prediction of ship motion under complex sea conditions not only plays a guiding role in the overall design of the ship but also is important for the ship's maneuverability and safety. Considering that ship motion state and trajectory prediction in wind and wave environments can support ship control and decision-making and reduce the overall operational risk of smart ships. In this paper, an adaptive order variation mathematical modeling (AOVMM) is developed for ship maneuvering motions under environmental changes by using the Taylor expansion and extended Kalman filter (EKF). To improve the prediction accuracy of the model, the order change of the hydrodynamic coefficients in the model is adapted to the environmental changes by the goodness of fit <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{R}^{2})$</tex>. The various maneuvers are cross-tested in different environments, using the optimal prediction model with calm water and wind and wave environments for predicting motion states and trajectories, respectively. The prediction results show that the proposed AOVMM can weaken the influence of the environment and significantly improve the accuracy of ship maneuvering motion prediction.

articleTitle: Acoustic Simulation Study of Subway Underwater Tunnels Based on EASE
abstract: The urban rail transit system is rapidly expanding due to its energy efficiency, ecological friendliness, and high capacity. However, the issue of noise pollution has received great attention. In order to solve the problem of excessive noise when subway tunnels pass through canals in specific cities, a sound field model was established using experimental data from existing subway systems. Calibrate the model until the simulation error is less than 3 decibels to verify its accuracy. This method will be applied to the sound field modeling of future target subway sections.

articleTitle: Underwater Wreck Detection Based on Mixed AnalogRealistic and Mixed Audiovisual Datasets
abstract: Facing the needs of marine archaeology and maritime emergency rescue for the detection of disaster targets, this paper improves the detection performance of existing algorithms for underwater disaster targets by establishing a hybrid analog/realistic dataset. Through the CycleGan network, maritime ship and aircraft photos are transformed into underwater ship and aircraft photos to simulate the wreck pictures obtained by the camera and sonar underwater. Combined with the audio and visual dataset traditional data enhancement methods, the hybrid dataset Unw of underwater disaster targets is established. Then the one-stage classical algorithm YOLOv5 is trained and tested on the Unw and Unw-vis consisting of photos taken by a single underwater camera, respectively. Comparison test results show that the model trained on Unw has improved the detection accuracy by about 0.25, the recall by about 0.249, the mAP50 by about 0.364, and the mAP50-95 by about 0.252 relative to the same model trained on the Unw-vis, indicating that the Unw and the proposed method are favorable for the application of underwater disasters detection.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-Based Formation Control for Multiple Unmanned Surface Vessels
abstract: This paper investigates the problems of formation keeping and translational control for unmanned surface vessels (USVs) in the presence of model uncertainties and external disturbances. Firstly, an adaptive sliding mode disturbance observer is introduced to estimate environmental disturbances. Based on the proposed observer, the system can effectively estimate unknown disturbances within a finite time without requiring the knowledge of the upper bounds of the disturbance and its derivative. Then, based on the state information of the neighboring vessels, the communication relationship between multiple vessels and the estimated value of the disturbance, a formation controller is designed using the auxiliary dynamic system and the dynamic surface method and to realize the USVs formation control under the disturbance of the external environment. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted to confirm the effectiveness of the controller and observer proposed for multiple unmanned surface vessels.

articleTitle: Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition via Combining Adaptive Line Enhancement and Deep Neural Network
abstract: Intelligent recognition of underwater acoustic targets is a crucial component of the intelligentization of underwater acoustic devices [1]–[3]. In recent years, with the development of computing technology, deep learning has become increasingly attractive in the recognition of underwater acoustic targets. Compared to traditional machine learning techniques, deep learning utilizes the strong nonlinearmodeling capability of deep neural networks, which enables the discovery of complex patterns hidden in large datasets and produces high-quality predictions or classification results [4], [5]. However, the complex acoustic channels, interference, and noise in the ocean often lead to the degradation or masking of some features of underwater acoustic signals, reducing the differentiation of signal characteristics between different types of targets. This, in turn, affects the capability of employed neural networks to extract features and classify underwater acoustic signals. Currently, the existing deep learning-based recognition methods of underwater targets are heavily influenced by noise and interference.

articleTitle: Subspace Detector of Multi-Frequency Signals Using the Single Hydrophone in Bottom Bounce Zone
abstract: Passive source detection is challenging in underwater acoustic signal processing. In this work, we consider the passive source detection using a single hydrophone in the Bottom Bounce (BB) zone in deep water. No prior knowledge about the ocean environment is assumed available, rendering the matched-field processing method to be unachievable. In this case, the classical Energy Detector (ED) can be used. It incoherently superimposes the energy of multi-frequency signals and declares the presence or absence of the source by comparing the signal energy to a prescribed detection threshold. While the ED's performance is highly limited by the low signal-to-noise phenomenon in this zone. This paper proposes a subspace detector that coherently accumulates the multi-frequency signals energy by exploiting the multipath arrival structure characteristics of BB signal. The detector realizes coherent accumulation of multi-frequency signals by projecting the signals into the proposed vector subspace, thus rejecting noises outside the subspace and improving the detection performance. The performance superiority of the proposed detector over ED is verified by simulation in a typical deep-water channel.

articleTitle: OFDM Underwater Acoustic Communication Receiver Based on Deep Learning
abstract: In complex underwater environment, underwater acoustic (UWA) channel estimation and equalization can effectively obtain channel information and thus recover transmitted signals at the receiving end, which is an important part of communication receiver. In recent years, deep learning (DL) methods have been applied to UWA communication. However, most research focuses only on channel estimation, rather than viewing communication receivers as a complete black box in an end-to-end manner. In this paper, an end-to-end UWA-OFDM communication receiver based on Transformer model is newly proposed, and also compared with fully connected deep neural network (FC-DNN) model and convolutional neural network (CNN) model. The experimental results show that the Transformer model has the lowest bit error rate (BER) among all these three methods with simple structure and fast running speed.

articleTitle: Underwater Object Localization and Detection of Square Shaped Target using Edge AI in Video Streams
abstract: Oceans sensors play a vital role in measuring parameters such as salinity, turbidity, and marine pollution caused by plastics and petroleum. The data collected from these sensors enables us to mitigate the adverse climate impacts and protect the economics, tourism, and fishing industries that rely on the ocean. Traditionally, Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) and Remote Operated Vehicles (ROVs) are deployed to record videos over extended periods in an effort to locate active and inactive sensor nodes or buoys in the ocean. The identification of these sensor nodes has become increasingly crucial in recent times. However, the post-processing of these vast datasets requires human intervention, leading to time-consuming analysis. In our work, we have aimed to streamline this process by employing an Edge AI device (NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier) to process recorded videos from a pool environment. We designed a square-shaped target customized to mimic ocean sensors or buoys and utilized the custom YOLOv5 model to detect the target frame by frame in a video. Furthermore, our research can be seamlessly integrated with advanced automation technology, incorporating robotic components and waterproof casings to enhance underwater object tracking applications.

articleTitle: Improved Space Clustering for Single-Carrier Underwater Acoustic Communications
abstract: Beamforming then equalization (BF-EQU) is drawing increased research attentions for underwater acoustic (UWA) communications deploying an array on the receiver side. Compared with conventional multichannel equalization without beam-forming, the BF-EQU scheme enjoys improved performance and/or reduced complexity. In this paper, we propose an im-proved BF-EQU scheme for single-carrier UWA communications. Our contribution lies in three aspects: first, Khatri-Rao (KR) subspace preprocessing is employed in direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation such that spurious DoAs can be mitigated; second, null-steering (NS) beamforming is used to form directional signals based on DoA estimations; last, a direct adaptive equalizer (DAE) enabled by improved proportionate normalized least mean squares (IPNLMS) algorithm is adopted to recover transmitted symbols from directional signals. The proposed receiver scheme was tested by numerical and experimental data, and the results showed it achieves extra performance gain over existing BF-EQU schemes.

articleTitle: A Guidance Method for a Small Unmanned Surface Vehicle Wireless Charging
abstract: A small unmanned surface vehicle (USV) usually carries a limited battery, and the mission duration is also limited. Wireless charging at sea is a way to extend the duration of USV. This work extends the study of developing a vector field-based guidance method for collision avoidance in the ship simulator. When the USV is in a vector field where near the charging station, the ship follows the vector field for guiding to touch the wireless charging plate. This vector field consists of a straight-line vector field and four circular vector fields in four quadrants to form a heading command to steer the ship. The feasibility of this work is tested by implementing the vector field guidance method into a ship simulator. In this work, the simulation considered wind, wave, and current influences on ship motions and combined the vector field-based guidance method to show the feasibility of the guidance method for USV wireless charging.

articleTitle: Development of a Multiparameter Sensor Chip for In-Situ Marine Ecological Monitoring
abstract: A multiparameter sensor chip has been developed for in-situ marine ecological monitoring. The silicon-based sensor chip consists of four functional areas was designed to measure the temperature, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{pH}$</tex> and concentrations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Z}{{\mathbf{n}}^{2 + }},\mathbf{C}{{\mathbf{d}}^{2 + }}$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{P}{{\mathrm{b}}^{2 + }}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{C}{{\mathrm{u}}^{2 + }}$</tex> in seawater simultaneously. The long-term, online and in-situ monitoring of these marine parameters is of great significance to predict ecological problems such as heavy metal pollution, seawater acidification and climate warming.

articleTitle: On Real-Time Underwater Acoustic Communication with a Prototype Modem Implementation
abstract: This study highlights a specific use case of underwater acoustic communication where the (soft) real-time requirement has relatively low impact on the system and communication performance requirements. The use case concerns acoustic monitoring, where a spectrogram of a two-minute time window is transmitted as an image. As real-time here means continuous time coverage (with some delay), this makes that the system has two minutes for computing the spectrogram, encoding the communication waveform and its transmission. It is shown that, after optimization, this requirement could eventually be met on a small general-purpose processor board using a high-level interpreted language, which is ideal for rapid prototyping. The showcase concerned a demonstration in and around the Black Sea harbour of Mangalia, Romania, in the framework of the European project in which the work was performed. Finally, some thoughts are given on further performance improvements and shortening the development cycle for research purposes.

articleTitle: Mapping the Deepest Natural Underwater Cave
abstract: The Czech Republic is home to the Hranice Abyss, the world's deepest natural underwater cave, a site extensively explored by a dedicated team of divers from a speleology group. Over the years, numerous studies have been conducted to unravel the cave's mysteries, delving into fields such as biology, hydrogeology, and geology. Mapping a cave of such vast dimensions and staggering depth poses formidable challenges, making the task hazardous, demanding, and timeintensive for a limited team of divers. In July 2022, the UNEXUP project was invited to explore and map the cave with its robot (UXl-neo), which contains many acoustic and optical sensors, used for navigation, localization, and mapping. Its unique control and dynamics allow the robot to successfully navigate through caves and flooded mines. This paper delves into the specifics of the six days of mission dives, offering insights into the mapping process, and presenting some of the results obtained from the entire cave.

articleTitle: Developing Human-in-the-Loop Digital Twin for Offshore Operations with Working Class Remotely Operated Underwater Vehicle
abstract: Remote Operating Vehicles (ROV) are widely used in offshore operations such as cable laying and structure inspection to reduce and minimize the human exposure risk. These operations are expensive and offshore companies are lately trying to mitigate further costs of re-doing operations due to pilot errors and hardware or software failures. This paper presents a simulator solution that aims to resolve the issue of expensive and risky in situ pilot training as well as provide a framework to generate significant data for further analysis and test algorithms before deploying to the real system. A virtual environment based on Unity3D and software for emulation of sensors and electrical devices were developed and paired with ROV control application used in real-world operations. Initial experiments were conducted by collecting and analyzing data on ROV operation between professional ROV pilot and pilots with different levels of skill and experience.

articleTitle: LSFT-GAN for Underwater Acoustic Target Signals Generation
abstract: Due to the scarcity of underwater acoustic target signal data, accurate and efficient generation of underwater acoustic target signals is of great significance for the study of acoustic properties of underwater acoustic targets. We propose a method based on LSFT -GAN for generating underwater acoustic target signals. The method focuses on the line spectral features (LSF) of the underwater acoustic target signals and enables controllable generation of LSF of the underwater acoustic targets from multiclass to multiclass. The generation experiments' results indicate that the generated samples possess significant LSF of the underwater acoustic target signals in the target domain, while retaining a small amount of LSF of the underwater acoustic target signals in the source domain. To evaluate the quality and diversity of the generated samples, we test and extract features from the generated samples using a reliable underwater acoustic target recognition model. The evaluation experiments indicate that the average recall of the four classes of generated samples is 96.9%. The feature clustering is evident, exhibiting good quality and diversity. The method based on LSFT -GAN for generating underwater acoustic target signals can significantly enhance the data on underwater acoustic target signals.

articleTitle: Benefits of Neural Network-based Receivers in Underwater Acoustic Communication Systems
abstract: In conventional orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) communication systems, channel knowledge on data subcarriers is obtained through linear interpolation of the estimated channel information on pilot subcarriers.
